matters.title: J. First Amendment to the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the design/construction of a Tennis Multipurpose Facility in the Travis Bryan Midtown Park
matters.body: Bryan City Council Second Regular Meeting
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Nov 12, 2024 - Bryan City Council Second Regular Meeting 
 Category 
 6. Statutory (Automatic Approval) Agenda - This agenda consists of items previously approved by Council action such as adoption of items that are part of an approved budget or capital improvement projects, first and only readings of ordinances, interlocal agreements, or action that is required by law or delegated to the City Manager. Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 J. First Amendment to the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the design/construction of a Tennis Multipurpose Facility in the Travis Bryan Midtown Park 
 Type 
 Action (Statutory) 
 Preferred Date 
 Nov 12, 2024 
 Absolute Date 
 Nov 12, 2024 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 18,250,000.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Bond Funds 
 Goals 

 Quality of Life 

 Economic Development 

 Summary: 
 On October 10, 2023, the City Council approved the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the purposes of designing and constructing the City’s tennis multipurpose facility in Travis Bryan Midtown Park. Since October 2023, the contractor and City representatives have reviewed multiple schematic design plans in an effort to meet Texas A&M University’s expectations and needs, while keeping the facility within budget. 

 The Design/Build Agreement is one of three current Agreements related to the facility. The other two agreements are: 1) an Interlocal Agreement (ILA) with Texas A&M University System (TAMUS), and 2) a combined Facility Management Agreement with Sports Facilities Management, LLC (SFM) for the operations and management of the facility and the Legends Event Center. At a future date, these other two agreements may need consideration by the City Council to amend certain aspects, such as the tennis multipurpose facility completion date. The ILA with TAMUS includes an annual $675,000 payment from TAMUS to the City; the TAMUS annual payment amount is about one-half of the City's annual debt service of $1.285MM. The ILA also includes the "Intended Use" of the facility allowing Texas A&M University (TAMU) to use the facility under certain conditions as addressed in Section 7 and Exhibit B of the ILA. Section 7.4 of the ILA states, "COB shall have exclusive use of the Facility for all times not scheduled in advance by TAMU or required to be used by TAMU due to a severe inclement weather event adversely affecting a regularly scheduled TAMU tennis team outdoor practice or scheduled outdoor NCAA match or Tournament." 

 The original Design Build Agreement has a construction budget of $17,000,000, which contains within the scope multiple phases including: Pre-Construction, Design Development, Construction Documents, and Construction. Presently, the estimated cost for the design and construction of the facility is $18,012,360, which includes an expanded parking area and related sitework estimate of $1,051,285. That is, with the recommended expanded parking lot, the proposed budget has increased. The expanded parking area includes roughly 145 spaces, drive aisles, heavy duty concrete for a fire truck turnaround, landscaping, electrical, etc. 

 The original Agreement has a Substantial Completion date of August 8, 2025. Because of the extensive design review, the Substantial Completion date is shifted to June 28, 2026, subject to weather, supply chain, and other variables. The extended Substantial Completion date also is contingent upon a notice to proceed (NTP) date of February 19, 2025. 

 The purpose of this Council Action Form is for the City Council to consider an Amendment to the Design/Build Agreement to address two topics: 1) an increased budget, and 2) a revised Substantial Completion date. The amended budget amount is proposed at $18,250,000, which includes the expanded parking area. The additional parking is recommended as it overlays a portion of the current temporary lot. The temporary lot is used on a regular basis for overflow parking to complement parking at the Legends Event Center and the Satellite Parking Lot. That is, for large and/or multiple events, additional parking is needed to accommodate visitors and guests to the Legends Event Center and other events in Midtown Park. The revised substantial completion date addresses the extensive schematic design process to keep the project within budget, while meeting the needs of Texas A&M. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 At the conclusion of the Design Development phase, the Contractor will submit a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) Proposal to the City based on the design phase documents. The GMP Proposal will be in accordance with the guidelines established by the City and delivered in the format specified by City in Exhibit “E” attached to the original Agreement. Based on the current design estimate, the expectation is the GMP will be within the amended budget amount. 

 Based on the latest information, the current design (including the additional parking), and the contractor’s review of market costs, City staff recommends approving the Amendment to the Design Build Agreement. The proposed Amendment increases the funding from $17,000,000 to $18,250,000 (inclusive of the additional parking) and extends the project Substantial Completion date from August 8, 2025, to June 28, 2026, subject to weather, supply chain, and other variables. While City-issued Bond Funds are the funding source for the design build project, the ILA with the TAMUS includes an annual payment from TAMUS to the City in the amount of $675,000 for the term of the ILA, which is a thirty (30) year term. 

 Note: The design/build budget does not include furniture, fixtures, and equipment (FF&E), which will be a City expense similar to the operations and maintenance of the facility. Staff intends to work with Sports Facility Management (SFM) to procure FF&E, as SFM can use their national buying power to secure competitive pricing, similar to their function during the construction of the Legends Event Center. 

 Options: 
 Approve the First Amendment to the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the design/construction of a Tennis Multipurpose Facility in the Travis Bryan Midtown Park 
 Modify and then approve the First Amendment to the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the design/construction of a Tennis Multipurpose Facility in the Travis Bryan Midtown Park; this option may require additional negotiations with the firm, further discussions with Texas A&M, and consideration at a future City Council meeting 
 Do not approve the First Amendment to the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the design/construction of a Tennis Multipurpose Facility in the Travis Bryan Midtown Park and provide staff direction

 Nov 12, 2024 - Bryan City Council Second Regular Meeting 
 Category 
 6. Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 M. Consider approval of a Plug & Play, LLC Supplemental Funding Agreement between the City of Bryan and the Greater Brazos Partnership, Inc. 
 Type 
 Action (Statutory) 
 Preferred Date 
 Nov 12, 2024 
 Absolute Date 
 Nov 12, 2024 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 350,000.00 
 Budgeted 
 No 
 Budget Source 
 General Fund 
 Goals 

 Economic Development 

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan, in collaboration with Texas A&M University System Innovation ("TAMUSI") and the Greater Brazos Partnership ("GBP"), has identified an innovation ecosystem infrastructure gap as a critical priority to help technology start-up companies in the defense and aerospace sectors accelerate their business activities in Aggieland. As such, Plug & Play, Inc., a global leader in technology start-up business acceleration based in the Silicon Valley, was targeted as a potential partner to fill this gap. Over the course of the last several months, TAMUSI and the GBP have coordinated with Plug & Play, LLC on a plan to bring Plug & Play, LLC to Aggieland. The Supplemental Funding Agreement, as presented for City Council consideration, is a key element of that plan - an economic development partnership between TAMUSI and the community via the GBP. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Because the City of Bryan is the home TAMUS RELLIS and because of the start-up business accelerator focus of Plug & Play, LLC, staff considers this economic development partnership to be of high value. As stated above, Plug & Play, LLC is a global leader in technology start-up business acceleration. The combined annual cost of the Plug & Play Agreements with TAMUSI and GBP is $1,500,000 annually for up to three (3) years. TAMUSI will fund $800,000 and the GBP will fund $700,000 annually. The City's investment in this economic development partnership with TAMUSI, under the Supplemental Funding Agreement with GBP, is $350,000 annually. GBP will fund the remaining $350,000. In return, GBP's agreement with Plug & Play, LLC requires Plug & Play, LLC to: locate its offices in Bryan; hire four (4) full time employees to staff those offices; and provide access to the data, assets, and other resources Plug & Play has to offer. Specifically, GBP's agreement with Plug & Play, LLC requires establishment of an Advisory Committee and utilization of Plug & Play's proprietary platform called the "Playbook". The Supplemental Funding Agreement requires that the GBP shall: 

 - for those positions on the Advisory Committee for the Aerospace and Defense Program, which GBP is entitled to occupy, allow Bryan to appoint two (2) of the four (4) members of the Advisory Committee for the Aerospace and Defense Program and 

 - through GBP’s right to access pursuant to their Plug & Play Agreement, provide to Bryan access to Plug and Play’s proprietary virtual platform called the “Playbook,” which allows members to track engagement with startups and other information. GBP shall designate Bryan, or an employee of Bryan if an individual must be named, as one of its representatives authorized to create a profile on the platform and gain access to it. 

 Furthermore, the Supplemental Funding Agreement establishes the following: 

 - Upon failure of GBP to fulfill any of the provisions of sections 1, 2, or 3 of this Agreement or any other breach of this Agreement, GBP shall refund to Bryan the amount Bryan paid under this agreement within thirty (30) days of Bryan’s demand for same. 

 - Bryan will reimburse GBP, within thirty (30) days of an invoice from GBP, $350,000 to cover its share of the cost of the Plug & Play, LLC Agreement. GBP will timely tender payment to Plug & Play, LLC in accordance with the terms of its agreement. At Bryan’s request, GBP shall furnish to Bryan an invoice along with documentation showing the annual payment of $700,000 has been made. 

 - The term of this Agreement is from December 1, 2024, through November 30, 2025. This Agreement will automatically renew for up to two (2) additional terms, unless terminated as provided herein. Either party may elect to terminate by sending the other party notice at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then current term. Renewal is subject to annual appropriation by the Bryan City Council. 

 Staff recommends approval of the Supplemental Funding Agreement.

 Options: 
 1. Approve the Supplemental Funding Agreement 
 2. Do not approve the Supplemental Funding Agreement 

 Attachments: 
 1. GBP Plug & Play COB 2024 Funding Agreement - available at the City Secretary's Office

 Summary: 
 City staff submitted a Decision Package (DP) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 to replace the golf cart fleet at the City Course. The DP was approved in an amount not to exceed $224,000. The four year lease to purchase agreement with the current fleet of carts was completed in October 2024. The golf carts are no longer under warranty and repair costs will be funded from the City Course operations & maintenance budget. If approved, the 70 cart fleet at the golf course will be replaced and the old carts will be traded-in. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 The current fleet of golf carts are out of warranty. The cost of repairs for the existing fleet in FY 2024 was $17,300. The estimated cost for repairs if carts are not replaced for FY 2025 is $27,500. Recurring issues with the carts include replacement of starters, batteries, steering racks, and throttles.

 The purchase price of the new Club Car Tempo golf carts is $434,000. The trade-in value of the existing fleet is $210,000, resulting in an outright purchase price of $224,000. The value of the current fleet will continue to decrease, while maintenance costs will increase the longer the carts are kept.

 Golf carts provide the City Course a steady revenue stream. The golf course generated $285,000 of revenue from cart rental fees in FY 2024. When the carts break down golfers are inconvenienced, resulting in harm to the City Course's image.

 A four-year lease to purchase option was presented with monthly payments of $5,208 over the course of 48 months totaling $249,984. The lease to purchase was not considered as an outright purchase is less expensive. 

 City staff recommends the approval of replacing the golf cart fleet at the City Course via an outright purchase and trade-in of the old fleet at a price not to exceed $224,000. 

 Options:

 Summary: 
 A Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Annual Contract for Parks Custodial Services was issued on October 24, 2023. Sealed proposals were submitted to the Purchasing Department on November 16, 2023. The City received responses from four (4) vendors. These vendors included Garcia Cleaning Service, PureService Corporation, Junction Five-0-Five, and Superior Commercial Cleaning. 

 City staff provided a thorough review of all proposals. Evaluation criteria included, but was not limited to, the overall cost proposal, references, relevant experience, and familiarity with the City of Bryan. City staff recommended to City Council that PureService Corporation of Southlake, Texas provides the best value for the City of Bryan. The City Council approved staff proceeding with the award at the December 12, 2023 meeting. 

 The initial term of this contract was one (1) year with four (4) additional one-year extension options pending approval by the City Council for a possible total of five (5) years. Contract extensions cannot include increases in unit bid prices. The cost to date for the first contract term set to expire on December 11, 2024, totals $130,860. Historical costs for these services on the previous contract for the last three years were $138,855 (FY2021), $142,870 (FY2022), and $139,580 (FY2023). 

 The scope of work included with this contract consists of general custodial services to be provided to twenty-two (22) locations throughout the parks system. The scope of work consists of, but is not limited to, full service to restroom facilities, pavilions, amphitheaters, and kitchen areas. Service to trash receptacles, barbeque pits, and the removal of ground trash is included within specifications. Trash liners and paper products are the responsibility of the contractor. Monthly pressure-washing of pavilion and restroom areas is required. The contractor also is responsible for pre- and post-cleanings of rented facilities that fall outside of scheduled service visits. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 After evaluation of overall job performance during the first term of this contract, staff determined PureService Corporation met or exceeded all contract terms. The contractor consistently provided a quality product, addressed identified deficiencies in a timely manner, and has a dedicated management team that takes pride in their service. Unit pricing remains consistent with the current market rates and the contract’s scope of work. 

 City staff recommends the City Council approve the first extension of this contract to PureService Corporation in the amount of $154,065 . 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the first extension of RFP No. 24-010 "Annual Contract for Parks Custodial Services” to PureService Corporation in the amount of $154,065

 Summary: 
 The Communications and Marketing Department, in conjunction with the IT Department, is seeking approval for Data Projections, Inc. to complete a comprehensive upgrade to the audio-visual system in Council Chambers. The current system is outdated, with components that are failing, out of warranty, and no longer supported by manufacturers. Data Projections, Inc. completed the previous, partial equipment upgrade in late 2015.

 Key Features of the Proposed Upgrade:
 Modern Audio-Visual over Internet Protocol (AV-over-IP) Infrastructure: Provides high-quality video distribution and seamless integration with the City’s broadcast and conferencing systems.
 Advanced Video Conferencing Capabilities: Incorporates Zoom Room functionality and automated speaker tracking cameras for virtual and hybrid meetings.
 Enhanced Audio System: Includes new microphones and speakers, along with a mix-minus audio setup for crystal-clear sound in both in-person and virtual environments.
 High-Quality Displays: Two (2) 136-inch Planar LED video walls to improve visibility for presentations.
 Support for Government Access Channel 16: Upgraded equipment will enhance the picture and audio quality of live meeting broadcasts and recordings.
 User-Friendly Controls: Crestron touch panels provide easy operation for Councilmembers and staff.
 Installation and Programming: Data Projections, Inc. will complete the full installation, integration, and programming of the new infrastructure to ensure a seamless transition and ensure components are functioning properly.
 Training and Support: Includes user training for City staff, comprehensive troubleshooting documentation, and a 3-year service agreement for ongoing support and preventative maintenance.

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 The Council Chamber’s current audio, visual, broadcasting, and recording system is outdated, with components that are failing, out of warranty, and no longer supported by manufacturers. During recent City Council and Planning and Zoning meetings, equipment failures have resulted in meetings be interrupted or broadcasts/recordings being substandard. Failing equipment not only disrupts the efficiency and effectiveness of public meetings but also undermines the City's commitment to transparency, accessibility, and professionalism.

 Staff respectfully requests the City Council approve the proposed Agreement with Data Projections, Inc. for the replacement of audio, visual, broadcasting, and recording equipment for the Council Chambers in an amount not to exceed $279,124.44. While this expenditure is not budgeted, the funding source, the Public, Educational & Government Television (PEG) Fund, is specifically restricted to these types of purchases.  On October 10, 2023, the City Council approved the Agreement for Design Build Services between the City of Bryan and SpawGlass Construction Corporation, Inc. for the purposes of designing and constructing the City’s multipurpose tennis facility in Travis Bryan Midtown Park. Since October 2023, the contractor and City representatives have reviewed multiple schematic design plans in an effort to meet Texas A&M University’s expectations and needs, while keeping the facility within budget.

Jones League, Abstract No. 26, adjoining the northwest side of HSC Parkway between South Traditions and Atlas Pear Drives, including 28.31 acres of land out of The Traditions Subdivision, being Lots 1R, 2R, and Common Areas One through Four in Phase 27, Lot 1R and Common Area One in Phase 30, Lot 1R and Common Area One in Phase 31, Lot 1A in Phase 32, and Lot 1 and Common Area One in Phase 33, in Bryan, Brazos County, Texas. 
 Type

 No

 No 
 Goals 

 Economic Development 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 The applicants, Schultz Engineering, LLC, on behalf of the property owners, Bryan Traditions LP, are requesting to amend a previously-approved Planned Development – Mixed Use District (PD-M) on 71.3 acres of land out of the John H. Jones League, including 28.31 acres of land out of The Traditions subdivision. Much of the land within the subject property remains undeveloped as vacant acreage, but has been partially developed with a variety of land uses including hotel, office, retail, and multifamily uses. Properties outside of this district, but within the vicinity, either remain as vacant acreage, or are developed with office and multifamily uses. Many of these properties also are zoned PD-M district. 

 In 2001, the Bryan City Council approved rezoning case no. RZ01-05 to establish the 790-acre PD-M zoning district referred to as The Traditions. Since 2001, land within the subject property has been involved in three amendments to this PD-M District, being RZ15-10, RZ16-20, and RZ19-20. Case no. RZ15-10 established the original 71.3-acre PD-M zoning district for the Lake Walk development. The following two amendments provided sign standards for The Stella Hotel and the surrounding properties. These amendment did not include the entire 71.3 acres. 

 The purpose for this request is to include additional land uses, and supplementary regulations for such uses, to guide future development in the Lake Walk master planned community. 

 The following uses are proposed for inclusion with this PD-M amendment: 
 Amusement Arcade; 
 Child Care – Class B; 
 Child Care – Class C; 
 Commercial Amusement; 
 Motor Fuel Retail; 
 Structured Parking Facility; and 
 Venue. 

 In addition to the new land uses above, the following supplementary regulations are proposed in this request: 

 A new regulation stating that any motor fuel retail use must comply with the underlying PD-M District development standards, and the supplementary regulations provided in Sec. 130-34(t) of the zoning ordinance. If these standards conflict or overlap, the stricter standard will apply. 

 Supplementary standards for structured parking facilities inspired by the requirements in the Midtown and Innovation Corridor zoning districts. 

 An amended standard to require a minimum 18-foot sidewalk/drive-scape/streetscape area along both sides of major accessways, with a graphic to specify the location of such major accessways. 

 In addition to the items described above, the proposed PD-M District will include the signage standards and graphics approved in cases RZ16-20 and RZ19-29, mentioned above. Thus, the requested zoning district will establish consistent zoning regulations throughout the entire 71.3 acres. 

 The case was originally scheduled for the Planning and Zoning Commission meeting on December 5, 2024. During the public hearing, it was discovered the acreage description for the case was incorrect. Therefore, the Commission voted to postpone consideration of this case to its December 19, 2024, regular meeting so accurate notice of the request could be given. 

 Analysis and Recommendation: 
 During its regular meeting on December 19, 2024, the Planning and Zoning Commission concurred with staff and unanimously recommends approval of this rezoning request. The Commission adopted the written staff report and analysis as the report, findings, and evaluation of the Commission. 

 In making their decision, the Planning and Zoning Commission found: 

 The amended PD-M District zoning is consistent with the adopted goals and land use policies set out in BluePrint 2040. This PD-M District will help guide the continued development of a master-planned community with an appropriate mix of residential and nonresidential uses. 

 The requested PD-M District zoning is consistent and appropriate with the zoning districts on adjacent properties and recent development trends in the vicinity. 

 The requested PD-M District will create consistent zoning regulations across the subject 71.3 acres for the Lake Walk master planned community. 

 The existing roadway network will be able to support the vehicular and pedestrian traffic associated with the existing development. While the request may slightly increase traffic volumes in the immediate vicinity, it will not adversely affect the safety and convenience of vehicular and pedestrian circulation in the vicinity. 

 Options: 
 approve the requested zoning change as recommended by P&Z and staff; 
 approve the requested zoning change with modifications, which may require rescheduling the request for consideration on a future City Council meeting agenda; 
 deny the requested zoning change; or 
 deny the requested PD amendment with prejudice, as provided for in Zoning Ordinance Section 130-42(i)(2): “If a request has been denied with prejudice, the same or similar request may not be resubmitted to the city for six months from the original date of denial.”

 location map and aerial photographs; 
 draft ordinance with exhibits;

 excerpt from December 19, 2024, Planning and Zoning Commission meeting minutes; 
 staff report to the Planning and Zoning Commission; and

 Summary: 
 A Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Annual Price Agreement for Custodial Services was issued on November 20, 2024. By the RFP deadline of December 17, 2024, the City received seven (7) responses meeting all requirements. Proposals were received from Crystal Clear Cleaning, LLC, Service First Janitorial, Ambassador Services, McLemore Building Maintenance, American Facility Services, Jani-King of Austin, and Myriad Elite National Facility Services. 

 The term of this proposed contract is for two (2) years with three (3) additional one-year extension options pending approval by the City Council for a possible total of five (5) years. Any contract extensions cannot include increases in unit bid prices unless through a duly executed change order. 

 The scope of work consists of, but is not limited to, full service to restroom amenities, servicing of all trash receptacles, vacuuming, mopping, dusting, wipe down of flat surfaces, polishing of elevator bright-work, cleaning of breakrooms, disinfecting of water fountains, spot cleaning of carpets, spot cleaning of walls, and interior entryway glasswork. Sweeping of exterior entryways and walkways are included. Floors are to be stripped plus waxed and all carpeted areas to receive extraction services twice annually. Trash liners, cleaning supplies, paper products, equipment, and storage of such material to be utilized during the course of work are the responsibility of the awarded contractor. 

 While the RFP included up to fourteen (14) facilities based on three separate groupings, the proposed contract includes nine (9) properties and two (2) groups. Groups are based on specific service needs, overall square footages to be maintained, accessibility restrictions, and location. In an effort to improve overall customer service to facilities, the RFP included additional locations added for consideration listed in Group 3. Unit pricing allows the City the authority to prorate services determined to be deficient during the course of work and provides the ability to properly manage to address possible budget constraints. 

 The historical costs for this contract scope for the last three years were $170,513 (2022 term extension), $168,323 (2023 term extension), and $153,607 (2024 term extension). Due to unit pricing having not increased during the current contract’s five-year term, costs of goods and services for the proposed scope of work has increased approximately five percent (5%) each year dating back to 2020, and consequently, the custodial service budget is underfunded for today’s market conditions .  A City staff evaluation team reviewed proposals in detail. Evaluation criteria included, but was not limited to, qualifications and experience, rates and expenses, methodology to complete the proposed scope, and references for projects of similar size. After review of proposals and the current budget, staff determined only Group 1 and Group 2 can be funded at this time. Group 3 properties were included into the proposal process in an attempt to improve facility conditions, but will continue to be maintained internally until additional funding is allocated. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 After conducting reference checks, evaluating cost proposals, and reviewing vendors’ relevant experience, staff determined Crystal Clear Cleaning, LLC (Bryan, Texas) will provide the best value for the City. Staff recommends the City Council award this proposed contract to Crystal Clear Cleaning, LLC for Group 1 and Group 2 only in the amount of $218,399.

While many of these components will be replaced under warranty, if they fail, the return merchandise authorization (RMA) process takes time.  Goals 

 Service 

 Quality of Life 

 Public Safety 

 Infrastructure 

 Summary: 
 The existing Fire Station Alerting (FSA) system notifies fire stations of active fire and emergency calls. The process begins when Brazos County 911 Dispatch (BC911) receives a call for Fire Services. Dispatchers enter the details into the Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) system, which determines which units are available and their locations. CAD then sends a signal to activate the PA system at the requested stations, along with an alert tone. Firefighters, upon hearing the alert tone, listen for audio from the dispatcher detailing the nature and location of the call. The requested units then respond, monitoring the radio for additional instructions while enroute. 

 Justification for Replacement: The current FSA system is over 15 years old, with some original components exceeding 25 years of service. It has reached its end-of-life (EOL), and repair parts are no longer available. Additionally, the system’s expansion capabilities are limited to adding only one more fire station. Given these limitations, replacing the system is critical to maintaining the safety and efficiency of fire operations. 

 Proposed Replacement System: The new system will be the Zetron Max FSA, which offers modernized features designed to extend the service life of the alerting system. Key improvements include: 

 Automatic Notifications and Alerts: BC911 will continue to receive calls and enter data into CAD, which will then interface with the Zetron Max FSA. The system will automatically notify and alert the requested fire stations, using automated voice dispatching (text-to-speech) to convey the call type and details. 
 Health and Safety Enhancements: The Zetron Max FSA will gradually ramp up the audio to the PA system to ease the impact of loud tones and prevent startling the firefighters, improving their response times and safety. The system also has the option to control in-station functions, such as turning on lights, opening bay doors, and shutting off gas to stoves. 
 Redundancy and Reliability: The Zetron Max FSA incorporates multiple layers of redundancy in its design, network, VHF radio, and BVWACS radio channels, thereby ensuring greater reliability. 
 Future Expansion: The system supports future upgrades, such as zone alerting, lighting systems that limit calls to specific units/rooms based on call type, and features to improve nighttime responses, such as speakers with soft lighting. Additional features, such as turnout timers and Unit Display Boards (color-coded for each unit), will further enhance the system’s functionality. 

 Conclusion: Replacing the current FSA system with the Zetron Max FSA will provide a modernized, more reliable, and safer alerting system for fire stations, ensuring timely responses and better protection for first responders. The system’s expandability also ensures it can grow with the needs of the community. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Approval of the purchase of the Fire Station Alerting (FSA) Equipment, which will replace the current end of life (EOL) fire alerting system equipment, will enhance response times and improve the safety of both first responders and the community, enabling a faster and more reliable reaction to active fire and emergency calls. 

 The Information Technology Department respectfully requests the Bryan City Council authorize approval of the purchase of Fire Station Alerting (FSA) Equipment. This enhancement allows the Fire Station Alerting (FSA) equipment to be modernized by replacing the current end-of-life (EOL) fire alerting system. The new system will enhance the efficiency, reliability, and safety of fire station operations. The purchase of the new FSA system is proposed to be funded from the FY25 IT Budget, in the amount of $182,000. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the purchase of Fire Station Alerting (FSA) Equipment 

 2. Do not approve the purchase of Fire Station Alerting (FSA) Equipment and provide staff direction

 Summary: 
 On March 17, 2025, Request for Bids (RFB) #25-025 (Burton Creek Water Treatment Building Repair) was issued allowing for improvements made to the Burton Creek Wastewater Plant Administration Building. The scope of this project includes demolition and replacement of water damaged exterior siding, window and door framing, insulation, sheetrock, and staircase. The scope also includes installation of guttering around the building and installation of a drip guard above the entry door to mitigate water intrusion into the building from rain. Goodwin-Lasiter-Strong serves as the architect for this project. 

 Two (2) sealed bids were received on April 9, 2025, from (1) B&B Plumbing and Construction, Inc. and (2) Prestige Maintenance Construction. After review of both bids, B&B Construction's bid was found cost-prohibitive and Prestige Maintenance's bid was submitted as a lump sum and did complete the bid schedule as required (failing to provide unit pricing and alternative pricing). 

 The received responses were reviewed by staff and Goodwin-Lasiter-Strong. City staff recommends rejecting all bids. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Water Services recommends the City Council reject all bids for RFB #25-025 (Burton Creek Waste Treatment Building Repair). A new RFB for this project will be released in anticipation of gaining greater market interest for the project. 

 Options: 
 1. Reject bids 
 2. Do not reject bids and provide staff direction

matters.title: D. Consideration, Discussion, and Possible Action to Approve a Contract for the Steele Store Substation Upgrade Project
matters.body: BTU Board of Directors Regular Meeting

 Category 
 4. Regular Session - This agenda consists of items requiring individual consideration by the Board of Directors. 
 Subject 
 D. Consideration, Discussion, and Possible Action to Approve a Contract for the Steele Store Substation Upgrade Project 
 Type 
 Action, Discussion, Information

 May 12, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes

 Discussion: 

 Steele Store Substation is a 138kV/12.47kV substation located at 11650 W SH21, Bryan, TX. The transmission portion of the station was converted from a 69kV substation to a 138kV substation in 2019. The 12.47kV portion of the station was scheduled for reconstruction at a later date to accommodate load growth in the area near the RELLIS Campus and provide alternate load serving capabilities between Snook Substation and Smetana Substation. The existing distribution portion of Steele Store Substation is 1950's vintage with obsolete equipment. This project will replace the existing distribution bus, switches, and breakers with new standard design and equipment resulting in increased reliability and a safer working environment. 

 Bid requests were issued March 2025. Six responses were received. Bid totals ranged from $1,444,969 to $2,182,884. Lambda Construction I, Ltd. of New Braunfels, Texas submitted the lowest total bid for this project. Lambda has built several substations for BTU in the past 5 years and has provided exceptional results that were within budget and on schedule. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 

 Staff recommends the BTU Board authorize the BTU Board Chair to sign the attached contract with Lambda Construction I, Ltd. in the not-to-exceed amount of $1,444,968.80 for the construction of distribution facilities at Steele Store Substation.

 Subject 
 D. Consider approving a Retail Water Service Area Agreement with Wellborn Special Utility District for an amount not to exceed $258,400 
 Type

 Summary: 
 In an effort to facilitate growth in and around the RELLIS Campus in northwest Bryan, staff negotiated an agreement with Wellborn Special Utility District (SUD) to purchase water service area (Water CCN (Certificate of Convenience and Necessity)). Staff identified approximately 4,800 acres as shown in Exhibit B as the "Joint Planning Area" to which this Agreement will be applicable. The specific transfer area identified in the agreement to be transferred immediately is the 323 acre tract located at SH47 and SH21 known as the Luza Tract as shown in Exhibit A. The timeframe for this Agreement is five years. The cost per acre for the CCN service area is set in year one at $800 per acre. The cost of the CCN service area adjusts on an annual basis based on the CPI (Consumer Price Index). 

 No later than thirty (30) days from the approval of this Agreement by both parties, both Bryan and Wellborn SUD agree to jointly file this Agreement with the PUC pursuant to Texas Water Code § 13.248. No later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, Wellborn SUD shall submit a request to the United States Department of Agriculture, Rural Utilities Service (“RUS”) requesting consent or non-objection by RUS to the transfer of the Transfer Area as contemplated by this Agreement (the “RUS Approval”). Bryan shall pay Wellborn SUD the Transfer Area Compensation Amount ($258,400) not later than thirty (30) days after receipt by Bryan of a copy of the RUS Approval. 

 The Parties identified the CCN area shown as the “Joint Planning Area” on Exhibit “B” whereby they agree to cooperate on retail water service planning, with the intent that Bryan will design infrastructure to become the primary retail water supplier, and in doing so will work to relieve Wellborn SUD of its future service obligations in the area. At any time during the Term, Bryan may provide written notice to Wellborn SUD that it desires a transfer of the Wellborn SUD Water CCN for all or a portion of the Joint Planning Area (each a “Transfer Notice”). However, any such notice must include the entirety of every requested tract of land, without reducing any tract size, or seeking the CCN area on only a portion of a tract, in an effort to shortchange the amount of payment due to Wellborn SUD. Following Wellborn SUD’s receipt of a Transfer Notice, the Parties agree to cooperate regarding the CCN transfer, including 1) preparation of a CCN transfer agreement, or amendment to this Agreement; 2) providing compensation to Wellborn SUD using the (adjusted) Base Compensation Amount; and 3) following the terms and procedures used by the Parties for the Transfer Area as to the basis for each transfer initiated by a Transfer Notice. 

 If at any time during the Term, Bryan provides a Transfer Notice that includes any existing Wellborn SUD customer or if Bryan has provided Transfer Notices that, when added to the Transfer Area, cumulatively request the transfer of the Wellborn SUD Water CCN for 75% or more of the area of the Joint Planning Area, then (in either case) the Parties shall cooperate to prepare a Customer Transition Plan, as part of the subject CCN transfer. The Customer Transition Plan shall set forth the timing and basis for Bryan to assume the retail service obligations from Wellborn SUD for all customers in the Joint Planning Area, and the amount of the mutually agreed compensation to Wellborn SUD for the loss of such customers and facilities. The additional compensation amount shall not be less than One Thousand Dollars ($1000) per residential customer equivalent (based on a 5/8 inch meter). Currently, 49 customers with 5/8 inch meters north of SH21 exist. 

 For the proposed transfer area (323 acres), the developer has agreed to reimburse the City for the purchase of the CCN area. This reimbursement may require a future agreement between the City and the Developer. 

 Staff recommends the City Council approve the proposed Agreement as presented to facilitate growth and future development around the RELLIS Campus and the northwest area of Bryan. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends the City Council approve the retail water service area agreement between Bryan and Wellborn SUD. This proposed Agreement will be the framework for which up to approximately 4,800 acres and 49 existing customers could be transferred to the City of Bryan for water service. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the Agreement
 2. Approve the Agreement with modifications, which may require consideration at a future meeting
 3. Do not approve the Agreement

 Attachments: 
 1. Retail Water Service Area Agreement
 2. Exhibit A
 3. Exhibit B

 Summary: 
 City of Bryan Well #16 is located on Louis Mikulin Road and currently does not pump water. Staff has not been able to determine if the existing pump has a problem, the water level is not sufficient to provide water to the pump, there is a physical problem with the well screening, or another problem within the well. In an effort to attempt to have the water well functional as quickly as possible, staff bid a menu of work items for a well contractor. Initially the well contractor will pull the pump, determine the water level in the well, video survey the well column, and visually inspect the existing pump to see if a defect exists. The bid includes for the contractor to rebuild the existing pump if feasible. The bid also includes the purchase of a new 9 stage pump; a new pump delivery is estimated at a minimum of 26 weeks from ordering. 

 The bid also allows for lowering the pump to provide increased pumping capacity. If the existing pump can be rebuilt, the new pump will be used as a replacement pump for either this well or other wells the City currently operates. The configuration of a new pump allows for the pump to be placed at a lower elevation in the well in anticipation of lower water levels in the future. 

 A provision exists in the bid for the well contractor to pump the well at 3000 gallons per minute (gpm) with their own equipment to determine the well capacity and screening. 

 Bids for this project were opened on April 25, 2025. Two (2) bids were received with Alsay, Inc submitting the lowest responsive bid. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends the City Council approve the construction contract for the rehabilitation of Well #16 to Alsay, Inc.

 Type 
 Action (Statutory)

 Jul 08, 2025 
 Absolute Date 
 Jul 08, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 4,495,303.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Transportation Fee Fund (Fund 240) 
 Goals 

 Infrastructure 

 Service 

 Summary: 
 The 2025 Street Maintenance Concrete contract includes street pavement repairs, sewer replacement, and drainage improvements along Waverly Drive, West 23 rd Street, and Wildflower Drive. This contract consists of three (3) bid items: one (1) base bid and two (2) alternate bids. 

 The base bid contains nine (9) streets (or ~ 4.63 lane miles) receiving substantial roadway repairs, drainage improvements, and sanitary sewer line replacement. All streets will be paved with 6-inch concrete, with four (4) streets converted from asphalt to concrete pavement. Reconstructing asphalt street segments into concrete will reduce long-term maintenance costs and increase the roadways life cycle. In addition to the base bid, two (2) alternate bids are included within this contract. Alternate Bid #1 includes pavement repairs and drainage improvements to a section of Wildflower Drive. Alternate Bid #2 includes an additional bid item to allow cement stabilized sand in lieu of lime stabilization for Waverly Drive and West 23rd Street to reduce the amount of disruption during construction to the residents. 

 To minimize risk or costly repairs, staff carefully coordinates work so subsurface utilities are addressed prior to street maintenance work. Pavement markings removed during construction will be replaced, once work is complete. (Please see attachments for a list of streets segments and location maps.) 

 As mentioned above, the base bid includes nine (9) streets to be repaired and paved in concrete, with drainage improvements along Waverly Drive and West 23 rd Street, and sewer replacement along a portion of West 17 th and West 23 rd Street. Streets receiving pavement repairs along sections (or portions) of the roadway include Carson Street, Cavitt Avenue, Sims Avenue, and Old College Road. Since lengths of these roadways are still in good condition, staff identified poor areas (and/or blocks) of the roadway to be repaired. Although the entire length of the roadway will not be reconstructed, damaged sections will be replaced creating an improved driving surface. To minimize traffic disruption along Cavitt Avenue, Sims Avenue, and Old College Road, a high early strength concrete will be used to reduce the curing time and should allow the roadway to be reopened sooner to traffic. 

 Three other streets within the base bid are Pendleton Drive, BRAC Road, and West 17 th Street. Pavement repairs along Pendleton Drive will be from Beacon Heights to the round-about at Oakmont Boulevard, which will include the pavement around the roundabout. This construction work will complete the conversion of the nine (9) foot wide asphalt road to concrete, from Boonville Road to the roundabout at Oakmont Boulevard. BRAC Road will be repaired and repaved from the Highway 6 service road to the Parks & Recreation maintenance shop. This work will include the road adjacent to the new BTU Admin Building from the service road to the intersection; and the asphalt road from the intersection to the Parks & Recreation maintenance shop. BRAC Road carries traffic entering and exiting all athletic fields located at Bryan Recreational Complex (or BRAC). Pavement repairs along West 17 th Street will be from Highway 21 to North Congress and include removal and replacement of approximately 840 feet of 6-inch sanitary sewer pipe. 

 Lastly, included in the base bid, will be two projects to improve drainage along Waverly (from Cavitt Avenue to South College Avenue) and West 23 rd Street (from Sims Avenue to Parker Avenue). During significant rain events, these roadways experience a high level of surface runoff and do not properly drain water from the roadway to storm inlets. To help drainage issues along Waverly Drive, the roadway will be inverted to direct water to the center of the road. The water will then be carried towards the newly installed storm inlets located at the corner of Waverly Drive and South College Avenue, with a small length of Waverly Drive directing water towards Cavitt Avenue. Similarly, along West 23 rd the roadway will be inverted, directing water to the center of the road. The water will then be carried towards Sims Avenue to an inlet at the corner of West 23 rd Street and Sims Avenue. Within the scope of the work along West 23 rd Street will be the removal and replacement of approximately 250 feet of 12-inch sanitary sewer pipe. 

 In addition to the base bid, this contract includes two (2) alternate bid items. Alternate Bid #1 includes pavement repairs and drainage improvements along Wildflower Drive from the concrete flume at 2900 Wildflower Drive to the intersection at Briarcrest Drive. This work will include installing additional drainage inlets, storm pipe, and converting the pavement from asphalt to concrete. Alternate Bid #2 includes an additional bid item to allow cement stabilized sand to be used instead of lime stabilization for Waverly Drive and West 23rd Street. Using cement stabilized sand should save construction time and allow for work to be completed timelier by the contractor. 

 Four (4) competitive bids were received for this contract. Larry Young Paving submitted the low bid at $4,495,303, representing the best value to the City. The total bid includes the base bid at $4,077,790.50, Alternate Bid #1 at $388,062.50, and Alternate Bid #2 at $29,450 for a total of $4,495,303. This contract is funded through the Transportation Fund with a budget from FY25 “Street Maintenance Projects”. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff respectfully requests the City Council award this construction contract for the 2025 Street Maintenance Repairs – Concrete to Larry Young for the not to exceed amount of $4,495,303. The Public Works Department has collaborated on the selection of street segments based on the age/condition of the streets, work orders submitted by residents, and the condition of subsurface utilities in order to use Transportation Fund most efficiently. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the proposed contract 
 2. Do not approve the proposed contract and provide direction to staff

Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 H. Approval of a Design Contract for a New Water SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) System to Brock Solutions for a not to exceed amount of $1,335,349 
 Type 
 Action (Statutory) 
 Preferred Date 
 Nov 11, 2025 
 Absolute Date 
 Nov 11, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 1,335,349.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Water Fund 
 Goals 

 Service 

 Infrastructure 

 Summary: 
 Water Services requests City Council consideration and approval of a contract with Brock Solutions (Brock) in the not to exceed amount of $1,335,349 for design of a new Water SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system. SCADA is a system of software and hardware used to monitor and control industrial processes. For this contract, the industrial processes include pumps, valves, instrumentation, and disinfection equipment used for production, storage, treatment, and delivery of drinking water to the end-user. Key elements of this contract include: (1) hardware modernization, (2) development of a new SCADA platform, (3) radio network upgrade, and (4) optimization of control and alarm strategies. 

 On April 1, 2025, Request of Qualifications (RFQ) #25-024 “SCADA System Improvements” was issued qualifying firms to upgrade the Water SCADA system. Fifteen (15) proposals were received and evaluated. The firm determined to be best qualified for this project was the response submitted by Brock Solutions in the not to exceed amount of $1,335,349. 

 Many components of the Water SCADA system are at end of life, or approaching end of life, which means they are no longer supported by or procurable from the manufacturer. Failure of a critical component could have significant impact on the City’s ability to produce and deliver water to its customers. Restored service requires a workaround solution until a permanent fix can be installed. The proposed contract addresses this concern by replacing end of life components with current technologies that are market available and manufacturer supported. 

 HMI, or human machine interface, refers to the system that allows a human operator to interact with a machine. The HMI takes the numerical information from SCADA (asset tags, run hours, asset condition, etc.) and illustrates them in a manner understandable by the operator. Services provided in this contract will redevelop the HMI to a new system platform (VTScada). The HMI graphics will meet current industry standards and will be expanded to include new Water System assets (such as Chick Lane Elevated Tower and Wells #20 and #21) allowing system control from a single platform. 

 The Programmable Logic Centers (PLCs), ruggedized industrial computers, serve as the "brain" for a specific automated process or machine. The PLCs and associated I/O (input and output) devices will be changed to a new platform. The I/O will bridge the gap between the physical process and the supervisory control software. As part of their contract, Brock will fabricate and deliver all required control panels and backplates for the system upgrade. Panels exhibiting deterioration and/or are undersized will be replaced with new. Factory Acceptance Testing and Hardware Factory Acceptance Testing is included in this contract. Testing programmed logic and installed hardware in a laboratory setting provides added assurance and confidence for a successful installation and project. 

 The current SCADA system is not able to operate in an automated state and is dependent upon human input. Improved automation will be gained by redeveloping the control strategies to operate with minimal operator input. This improvement will free up resources and allow staff to focus attention on other needs in the water production system. 

 Lastly, construction services are included in this contract, including construction bid package development, submittal review, training, and start-up and commissioning. Brock Solutions also can provide the planned construction services and will have the opportunity to bid on the installation construction contract at a later date, and the result of the bid will be presented to City Council for consideration. 

 An estimated 567 days is forecasted for project completion. 

 The presented contract allows for 4 major deliverables:

matters.body: Bryan City Council Second Regular Meeting
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Aug 12, 2025 - Bryan City Council Second Regular Meeting 
 Category 
 5. Consent (Automatic Approval) Agenda - This agenda consists of ministerial or “housekeeping” items required by law such as routine bids, contracts, purchases, and resolutions. Items may be removed from the consent agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 B. Approval of the proposed contract with TK Elevator Corporation (TK) in the amount of $119,882.37 that will allow for the modernization of the Phillips Event Center Elevator 
 Type 
 Action (Consent) 
 Preferred Date 
 Aug 12, 2025 
 Absolute Date 
 Aug 12, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 119,882.37 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 General Fund (Approved Decision Package for Fiscal Year 2025) 
 Goals 

 Quality of Life 

 Infrastructure 

 Service 

 Summary: 
 The Phillips Event Center facility consists of a single Otis hydraulic passenger car elevator system that supports the two-story facility. The unit is original and was placed into service circa 1987. The unit is currently operational, but has exceeded its life expectancy. With the units age along with deteriorating mechanical components, the elevator is becoming obsolete. Based on the age and history of the elevator, staff anticipates extended downtimes due to mechanical issues, excessive lead times on replacement parts that may no longer be manufactured, and increased liability exposures due to outdated life safety components. 

 Proposals were received from two (2) reputable elevator modernization companies. After reviewing the proposals, staff recommends the proposal submitted by TK Elevator Corporation (TK) provides the best overall value to City, while remaining within the Fiscal Year 2025 Decision Package amount of $144,000. 

 Included in the scope of work is a new controller, car door, car fixtures, pit equipment, jacks, hydraulic power unit, and all hoist way equipment. The interior of the car will not be upgraded as it is in good condition, including recently installed flooring. 

 At the request of City staff, the proposal also incorporates a turnkey approach, including labor and materials, to address any code deficiencies beyond the general elevator modernization base scope. This work typically is the responsibility of the owner to address before mobilization of the elevator contractor. These requirements include configuration of the fire alarm system, electrical work, and any other general construction upgrades to meet current State licensing regulations. The turnkey approach will assist in streamlining the project as the vendor will be responsible for coordinating, scheduling, and managing all trades to address the related work reducing the possibility of demobilizations or delays caused by third-party vendors. 

 The proposal also allows for a five (5) day turnaround for project completion versus the industry standard estimate of four (4) to six (6) weeks. As the Phillips Event Center is a 7-day a week operation, which includes the City Course and the restaurant along with special events, the 5-day turnaround provides a higher degree of success in having the project's completion expedited. 

 TK is a current service provider with Omnia Partners where contracts are competitively solicited and publicly awarded, which allows the City of Bryan to utilize pre-established contract prices. As previously stated, the proposal amount is within the approved FY 2025 Decision Package budgeted amount of $144,000. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 After review of proposals, staff recommends the City Council approve awarding the Modernization of the Phillips Event Center Elevator Contract to TK Elevator Corporation (TK) in the amount of $119,882.37. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the contract with TK Elevator Corporation in the amount of $119,882.37 allowing for the modernization of the Phillips Event Center Elevator 

 2. Do not approve the contract with TK Elevator Corporation allowing for the modernization of the Phillips Event Center Elevator and provide staff with direction

 Subject 
 A. Rezoning request case no. RZ25-03, public hearing, presentation, and consideration of the first and only reading of an ordinance of the City of Bryan, Texas, amending Chapter 130, Zoning, of the City of Bryan Code of Ordinances, by changing the zoning classification from Planned Development – Mixed Use District (PD-M) to Planned Development – Housing District (PD-H), on 20.398 acres of land out of the J. W. Scott League, Abstract No. 49, located at the north corner of Boonville Road (FM 158) and Copperfield Drive in Bryan, Brazos County, Texas. 
 Type 
 Action 
 Preferred Date 
 Aug 12, 2025

 Aug 12, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 No

 No

 na 
 Goals 

 Economic Development 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 The applicants, Kimley-Horn and Slate Real Estate Partners, on behalf of property owner Adam Development Properties, LP, are requesting to change the zoning classification on 20.398 acres of land from Planned Development – Mixed Use District (PD-M) to Planned Development – Housing District (PD-H) in order to provide development opportunities for an apartment development. The applicants’ proposal includes standards to guide multiple-family residential development that could result in up to twelve (12) multifamily dwelling buildings, and includes regulations for architectural standards, landscaping requirements, natural area preserves, and building height maximums.

 Since the approval of the current PD District zoning on the subject property in 2015, there have been several rezoning requests regarding this acreage. 

 Case no. RZ22-18: A request to amend the PD-M District zoning on about 18.5 acres of these 20.3 acres to include multi-family residential and townhome uses, and to reserve a 1.86-acre portion of this tract for retail use. Prior to scheduling the request for a Planning and Zoning Commission (P&Z) hearing, the request was amended by the applicants to request Multiple-Family (MF) District zoning. Staff recommended denying the requested MF District zoning and the case was withdrawn by the applicants prior to the P&Z meeting.

 Case no. RZ23-08: A request to rezone the subject property from PD-M District to PD-H District in order to utilize the entire property for a multi-family residential development. P&Z recommended denial of the proposal by a vote of five (5) to three (3) during its June 1, 2023 meeting. At the time, Commissioners remarked that the apartment building proposal did not meet the intent of the Future Land Use Plan and a retail component may be a better use.

 Case no. RZ23-30: A request to amend the existing PD-M District, to allow multi-family and retail development. Prior to the P&Z hearing, the applicants withdrew the request to allow time to review and respond to citizen feedback.

 Case no. RZ24-09: A resubmittal of the previously-withdrawn case (no. RZ23-30). During the P&Z’s public hearing on April 4, 2024, six (6) citizens spoke in favor of the request and nineteen (19) citizens spoke in opposition. Those in opposition expressed concerns about the perceived increase in density and traffic and the effect on the local elementary school.

 Following the public hearing, the Commission voted to recommend approving the request by a vote of eight (8) in favor to one (1) in opposition. The Commission’s positive recommendation in this case was made subject to the following modifications to the proposal:

 Remove “Planning Area 2”, which was intended to follow standards of Bryan’s Retail District (C-2);
 Remove the proposed underground detention; and
 Add an above-ground detention pond in the area where “Planning Area 2” was previously shown.

 During the City Council’s public hearing on June 18, 2024, thirteen (13) citizens spoke in opposition to the request and six (6) citizens spoke in favor. Following the public hearing, City Council voted to deny the request by a vote of six (6) in favor to one (1) in opposition, citing concerns the proposal did not comply with the Comprehensive Plan and current traffic facilities did not generally appear suitable or adequate for the proposed multi-family residential use. An excerpt from the City Council’s June 18, 2024, second regular meeting minutes is attached to this staff report as Exhibit “C”. 

 The purpose of this current request, referred to as case no. RZ25-03, is to provide development opportunities for a planned apartment development. The development plan is attached to this staff report as Exhibit “B”. The current rezoning request is identical to the most-recent rezoning request considered by City Council in June 2024. (case no. RZ24-09). 

 The proposed development regulations represent several departures from standard MF District site requirements, including:

 Specific outdoor lighting levels intended to prevent any glare or light spilling onto adjacent residential subdivisions.
 Building material and design requirements. Proposed residential and amenity buildings are proposed to have both expression of structural elements (i.e. columns), variations in wall planes, as well as changes in material, pattern, and color. Natural stone, brick, wood, and decorative exposed concrete will be utilized as façade materials. 
 Building height transitions. Adjacent to the Miramont Subdivision building height is proposed to transition down from 50 feet to 35 feet. 
 Natural area preserve (4.34 acres), which serves as a buffer from adjacent residential districts.
 All new required landscaping is proposed to be installed in landscape zones adjacent to Copperfield Drive and Boonville Road (FM 158). 

 The only primary land use proposed on the subject property with this request is apartment buildings. Adjacent properties located to the north, east, and west are also zoned PD-M District and are part of the Miramont Subdivision, including a portion of the Miramont Country Club Golf Course. Properties located to the south, southeast, and southwest are zoned Retail District (C-2).

 Analysis and Recommendation: 
 During the Planning and Zoning Commission’s public hearing on July 17, 2025, two (2) citizens spoke in favor of the request and nine (9) citizens spoke in opposition to the request. Those in opposition expressed concerns about the perceived increase in density and traffic and the effect on enrollment at the local elementary school. 

 Following the public hearing, the Commission voted to recommend approving the request by a vote of five (5) in favor to two (2) in opposition. The Commission adopted the written staff report and analysis as the report, findings, and evaluation of the Commission.

 The Planning and Zoning Commission finds that:

 While BluePrint 2040 suggests the subject property is within an area suitable for retail uses, the Commission identifies that high density residential development also are suggested to be located on major collector or arterial street and medium and high density residential should be used as a transition to adjacent low density residential areas.

 This PD District provides for height transition, natural area preserve, and landscape zones, which provide a context sensitive and carefully designed pattern of urban growth and development.

 Options: 
 approve the requested zoning change as recommended by the Planning and Zoning Commission;
 approve the requested zoning change with modifications, which may require rescheduling the request for consideration on a future City Council meeting agenda; 
 deny the requested zoning change; or
 deny the requested zoning change with prejudice, as provided for in Zoning Ordinance Section 130-42(i)(2): “If a request has been denied with prejudice, the same or similar request may not be resubmitted to the city for six months from the original date of denial.”

 Attachments: 
 location map and aerial photographs;
 draft ordinance with exhibits;
 excerpt from July 17, 2025, Planning and Zoning Commission regular meeting minutes;
 staff report to the Planning and Zoning Commission;
 staff report exhibit attachments (separate PDF);
 written comments received concerning the RZ25-03 rezoning request on this subject property (separate PDF); and

Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 F. Award the Fiscal Year 2026 Excess Liability Policy for Bryan Texas Utilities (BTU) to AEGIS for an annual premium not to exceed $253,696. 
 Type

 Sep 09, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact

 Dollar Amount 
 253,696.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Fiscal Year 2026 Budget - BTU 
 Goals 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan has General Liability, Law Enforcement Liability, Errors & Omissions Liability and Auto Liability with the Texas Municipal League Intergovernmental Risk Pool (TMLIRP). These coverages are being considered in a separate Council Action Form. This Council Action Form seeks to award Excess General Liability and Auto Liability for Bryan Texas Utilities (BTU) specific exposures.

 The current liability policy through TMLIRP has a $500,000 deductible and provides various limits. That is, if a claim exceeds $500,000, TMLIRP will cover $2,000,000 per occurrence/$6,000,000 aggregate for General Liability, $3,000,000 per occurrence/$6,000,000 aggregate for Law Enforcement Liability, and $2,000,000 per occurrence/$4,000,000 aggregate for Errors & Omissions Liability. Fiscal Year 2025 was the first year this proposed policy was procured with an annual premium not to exceed $230,758. This policy is in excess of the TMLIRP policy limits (for BTU-related exposures only), and will provide an additional $5,000,000 per occurrence under General Liability for a total of $7,000,000 per occurrence between both policies, and an additional $5,000,000 under Auto Liability for a total of $8,000,000 per occurrence. The proposed policy has a wildfire exclusion, and is intended to cover only BTU operations. The total premium for the proposed coverage for Fiscal Year 2026 is $253,696 for a 9.94% increase over expiring, which is the lower end of trend increases applied across the AEGIS book of business. The initial indication from the market was a 22.5% increase; however, the City's Broker of Record, Alliant Insurance Services, Inc., re-negotiated resulting in minimizing the increase to 9.94%. 

 AEGIS is a mutual insurer formed in 1986 by utilities when the commercial marketplace stopped providing capacity and coverage terms meeting the needs of utilities. Nuclear verdicts and catastrophic risk exposures within utilities as well as their proprietary function status, solidify the need for additional coverage for Bryan Texas Utilities (BTU).

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 The City's Sole Broker of Record, Alliant Insurance Services, did a market check, and along with City staff, reviewed the proposed quote from the incumbent. The proposed coverage will continue to provide coverage for BTU-related exposures and provides a degree of protection in the event of a catastrophic loss. The renewal quote is favorable and in line with the current market. 

 Staff respectfully recommends award of Excess Liability Insurance to AEGIS with a $5,000,000 limit for BTU-related exposures at an annual premium of $253,696 for the policy period beginning October 1, 2025, and ending September 30, 2026. 

 Options: 
 1. Award Excess Liability Coverage for utility related exposures to AEGIS at an annual premium of $253,696 for the FY2026 policy period. 
 2. Do no award the Excess Liability Coverage for utility related to AEGIS and require staff to request additional proposals. Note: this will require action at a future City Council Meeting. 
 3. Do not award the Excess Liability Coverage for utility related exposures to AEGIS and provide direction to staff. Note: not awarding the policy could increase BTU's financial exposure.

 Goals 

 Service 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 Since 2002, the City has outsourced landscape management and mowing services as the cost to provide the service in-house is determined to be greater than obtaining the same services from an outside contractor. The intent of these contracts is to cost-effectively maintain and operate the parks and open space network in a manner that provides safe, clean, attractive, and orderly parks and facilities, while promoting optimum utilization of the park system by citizens and visitors of Bryan. 

 With the current contracts expiring on October 18, 2025, Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 25-036 “Annual Price Agreement for Parks and Facility Landscape Maintenance Groups 1-6” was released on June 25, 2025. Six (6) responses were received from the following: Grassmasters, Roots Landscaping LLC, Landmark Landscape Group, Yellowstone Landscape Central Inc., Green Teams, Inc., and EMT Lawn Care DBA Major Landscaping. 

 The contract for landscape services is a comprehensive service contract. The contractor performs all work necessary utilizing acceptable horticulture practices for the exterior landscape maintenance of the properties. The contract term is for one (1) year with the option of four (4) one-year extensions awarded one year at a time for a possible total of five (5) years. Any extension shall require approval by the City Council and shall not include any increase in unit bid pricing, unless authorized through a duly executed change order. 

 Services include, but are not limited to: 1) mowing, edging, trimming, and blowing of turf areas; 2) litter collection/disposal; 3) fertilizer/herbicide application; 4) planting and maintenance of landscaped beds; 5) tree pruning, trimming, and shaping; and, 6) irrigation inspection and repairs, etc. 

 The scope of work is divided into six (6) individual groups. Bidders had the opportunity to bid on one, multiple, or all groups. Each group was assigned a Schedule A, B, or C, which relates to the frequency at which properties are serviced during the growing season: Schedule A properties are serviced twice per week, Schedule B once per week, and Schedule C once every two weeks. A general description of properties found within each group and correlating schedule is below: 

 Group 1 (Schedule A): Bryan Regional Athletic Complex (sports fields) 
 Group 2 (Schedule B): Parks 
 Group 3 (Schedule B): Facilities 
 Group 4 (Schedule B): Landscaped Right-of-Ways (ROW) and medians 
 Group 5 (Schedule B): Midtown Park 
 Group 6 (Schedule C): Green spaces and miscellaneous properties 

 The current contracted amounts for landscape maintenance services total $1,014,895. The cost for the last four (4) fiscal years for landscape maintenance services totaled: $739,665 (2022), $788,828 (2023), $756,736 (2024), and $609,102 (FY2025, to date). The contract amounts recommended by staff are within the total budget amount of $1,231,500 for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 An evaluation team consisting of City staff rated each proposal on four (4) categories: 1) Qualifications and Experience; 2) Rates and Expenses; 3) Methodology including technical approach and understanding of the scope of the project; and 4) references from contracts of similar scope. 

 The companies being recommended are currently contracted with the City of Bryan for either right-of-way mowing, lawn maintenance of water production/waste-water treatment plants, City parks, City facilities, or other City-owned properties. The three (3) recommended companies have received positive references from staff overseeing the individual scopes of work. 

 After evaluating all submitted proposals, staff recommends awarding contracts to Yellowstone Landscape Central Inc. for Groups One (1), Two (2), Three (3), and Five (5) in the amount of $726,908.38; Green Teams, Inc. for Group Four (4) in the amount of $90,867; and Grassmasters for Group Six (6) in the amount of $39,195. A s recommended, the proposed total cost ($856,970.38) is $157,924.62 or over fifteen percent (15%) less than the current year budget amount of $1,014,895. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve awarding contracts for RFP #25-036 “Annual Price Agreement for Parks and Facility Landscape Maintenance Groups 1-6” to Yellowstone Landscape Central Inc. for Groups One (1), Two (2), Three (3), and Five (5) in the amount of $726,908.38; Green Teams, Inc. for Group Four (4) in the amount of $90,867; and Grassmasters for Group Six (6) in the amount of $39,195 for a total amount of all three contracts being $856,970.38 

 2. Select other combinations of contracts, which will require additional discussions with firms and consideration at a future City Council meeting 

 3. Do not approve awarding the contracts and provide staff with direction

 C. Consideration of a Life Safety Grant request for the installation of a fire suppression system, fire alarm, and egress stairs in the amount of $50,000 for an eligible property located at 101-103 North Main Street in Downtown Bryan, Brazos County, Texas.

 Summary: 

 On June 7, 2016, the Bryan City Council adopted a resolution establishing the Life Safety matching grant program. The intent of the program is to aid downtown business owners in the rehabilitation and restoration of Historic Downtown Bryan by utilizing a Chapter 380 economic development agreement. 

 An application for Life Safety Grant (LSG) funding in the amount of $57,100.00 was made by Emily Runnion on behalf of the property owner, W.F. Gibbs & Son LLC, on August 8, 2025, for their property at 101-103 North Main Street. 

 101-103 North Main Street is the location of Harvest Coffee Bar and a vacant office space previously the location of O’Connor & Associates Attorneys at Law. The new property owner intends to renovate the existing structure to provide additional retail and commercial space. The proposed interior renovations include the following life safety improvements required by the International Building Code and International Fire Code. 

 Installation of fire suppression system (2021 IFC Section 903).
 Installation of two (2) new fire stairways (2021 IFC Section 1011); and
 Installation of fire alarm and detection system (2021 IFC Section 907).

 After receiving all appropriate application materials (see attachments), the Life Safety Grant Review Panel reviewed the submission and determined the request met all applicable eligibility requirements. The panel recommends approval of a grant request for $50,000, the maximum reimbursement permitted by the program’s guidelines, which covers 35% of the total cost of life safety improvements proposed with the renovations on the property at 101-103 North Main Street.

 The City’s Grant Review Panel considers funding recommendations based on how well applications meet the criteria for funding as established in the Program’s guidelines. These criteria include (but are not limited to) the efficient use of dollars, increase to ad valorem and sales tax, creation of jobs, and the overall impact of the project. The City Council determines the final monetary allocation for grant applications, up to $50,000 per property. 

 In addition to this request, the applicant has applied for $50,000 in funding from the Downtown Improvement Program. Both requests are being considered for City Council approval on this agenda.

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Due to the older construction of the building, retrofitting structures with modern day safety systems and features, in this case, fire suppression systems, alarms, and egress stairs, can be costly and more labor intensive than for newer construction commercial buildings. To support the renovation of the space, the Grant Review Panel offers the following recommendation totaling in $50,000:

 101-103 North Main Street – $50,000 (100% of reimbursement request, program maximum) Life Safety improvements for 101-103 North Main Street, including installation of a fire suppression system, fire alarm system, and egress stairs, are required to bring the business and building into compliance with current fire and building codes. In return, the currently-vacant spaces within the building will be available for use by retail or commercial tenants. The installation costs are estimated at $141,427.25 without grant funding.
 Improvements to the safety features of this building in Downtown Bryan will increase property values; increase the economic vitality of buildings; potentially increase sales tax revenue if utilized by a retail tenant; and improve safety of buildings for the general public, business owners, and for first responders. 

 Options: 
 approve the life safety grant request for $50,000, as recommended by the Life Safety Grant Review Panel;
 approve the life safety grant request with modifications to the amount of funding, not to exceed $50,000 total (which may require City Council consideration at a future council meeting); or
 deny the life safety grant request and provide direction to staff.

matters.text:
