 Category 
 6. Statutory (Automatic Approval) Agenda - This agenda consists of items previously approved by Council action such as adoption of items that are part of an approved budget or capital improvement projects, first and only readings of ordinances, interlocal agreements, or action that is required by law or delegated to the City Manager. Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 BB. Consideration of a contract for professional services in an amount not to exceed $400,000 with Halff Associates, Inc. to prepare a new comprehensive plan for the City of Bryan 
 Type 
 Action (Statutory) 
 Preferred Date 
 Sep 09, 2025 
 Absolute Date 
 Sep 09, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 400,000.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 City Council approved $250k from the General Fund for this project for Fiscal Year 2025; additional funding from the General Fund is proposed in the City’s Fiscal Year 2026 budget. 
 Goals 

 Service 

 Quality of Life 

 Public Safety 

 Infrastructure 

 Economic Development 

 SUMMARY: 
 The Texas Local Government Code requires Texas cities that have enacted zoning, as Bryan did in 1989, to adopt zoning regulations in accordance with a comprehensive plan. The City’s current Comprehensive Plan, BluePrint 2040, was adopted on October 25, 2016. Many of that Plan’s action items, goals, and objectives are still valid. However, they need to be reviewed, evaluated, and updated to reflect citizens’ priorities, and to provide a current community assessment and implementation strategies to help guarantee quality, sustainable future growth. 

 Since 2016, the City has experienced significant private and public development-related activity. While some of this activity was partially considered in the 2016 Plan, many developments could not have been anticipated at the time. Significant developments and City initiatives during the last nine (9) years that affect city growth, development, and sustainability include, but are not limited to, the following: 

 Texas A&M University’s RELLIS Campus; 
 Innovation Corridor Zoning and Overlay Districts; 
 Texas Triangle Industrial Park; 
 Travis Bryan Midtown Park; and 
 Midtown Area Plan and Zoning Districts. 

 During a joint subcommittee meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission and City Council on March 5, 2024, the City Council instructed staff to begin the process of preparing a new comprehensive plan. The City released Request for Qualifications (RFQ) #25-009 on November 19, 2024, and received ten (10) sealed Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) on January 21, 2025. A selection committee comprised of City staff as well as representatives from the Planning and Zoning Commission, Parks Advisory Board, and City Council reviewed all submittals and interviewed three (3) consultant teams on March 26, 2025. 

 The selection committee determined the experience displayed and project methodology proposed by Halff Associates, Inc. (“Halff”), a Texas corporation, is the approach best aligned with the City’s goals for this comprehensive plan project. Subsequently, the City negotiated the professional services contract attached to this Council Action Form with a total contract fee in an amount not to exceed $400,000. 

 With this contract, the consultants are tasked to develop a new comprehensive plan for the City of Bryan. The revised project scope emphasizes the preparation of a community-wide comprehensive plan focused on future land use, neighborhoods, mobility, economic development, and implementation strategies. The final draft plan is scheduled for completion by October/November 2026, with anticipated City Council consideration and adoption in January/February 2027. The new plan will provide a guide for future decision-making to promote high-quality, orderly growth, development, and redevelopment of the community consistent with the vision and values expressed by residents, businesses, and stakeholders. 

 In the original scope, the project also included an update to the 2016 Parks, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan. That component has been removed from the revised contract, and the plan will no longer include a comprehensive assessment of park facilities, level of service standards, or trail network expansion strategies. Instead, the plan will concentrate on the core elements of a comprehensive plan while acknowledging that future parks and recreation planning may be undertaken separately. 

 The contract continues to require a robust public engagement and communications strategy. The project team will work with City staff to implement a comprehensive engagement program to identify target audiences, outreach methods, timelines, and responsibilities. This strategy will better ensure broad participation from residents, community groups, and stakeholders and will document feedback effectively throughout the planning process. 

 ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATION: 
 The selection committee recommends approving a contract for professional services with the Halff consultant team to develop a new comprehensive plan for the City of Bryan. 

 A comprehensive plan is the City’s principal guide in promoting orderly growth, development, and redevelopment of the City consistent with the vision, values, goals, and objectives established by the community. 

 The selection committee determined the experience displayed and project methodology proposed by Halff, a Texas corporation is the approach best aligned with the City’s goals for this comprehensive plan project. 

 OPTIONS: 
 approve the negotiated professional services contract in an amount not to exceed $400,000; 
 request modifications to the proposed professional services contract, which will require additional negotiation with the selected consultant and revised contract consideration during a future City Council meeting; or 
 do not approve this professional services contract and provide direction to staff. 

 ATTACHMENTS: 
 Contract for professional services for City of Bryan Comprehensive Plan with attachments; 
 Halff Statement of Qualifications in response to RFQ No. 25-009; and 
 RFQ No. 25-009.

Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 A. Approval of a professional services agreement with St. Joseph Physician Associates d/b/a St. Joseph Health Medical Group for the management and operation of an employee health center in an amount not to exceed $796,631 in the first year, with a possible 2.6% increase in subsequent years.

 Budget Source

 Goals 

 Service 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan Employee Health Center has been operational since March 31, 2011. Initially, the City was the sole participant in the partnership with St. Joseph Regional Health Center until Bryan Independent School District (BISD) joined through an Interlocal Agreement and began receiving services through the Center in January 2016. The Interlocal Agreement (ILA) established cost sharing between the City and BISD and remains in effect. In December of 2022, the City Council approved a separate ILA allowing the Brazos County Emergency Communications District (BC911) to obtain limited services through the Center beginning in January 2023. BC911 was charged annually based on the number of covered lives (approx. 62) to utilize the Center. In January 2025, BC911 withdrew from receiving services at the Center due to a change in insurance plans/structure. 

 Currently, operating costs for the Center are paid equally between the City of Bryan and BISD, with the exception of costs for services only the City receives through the Center (e.g. drug screens, rabies vaccines). In addition to the services provided at the Center, through an agreement between St. Joseph Health System (SJHS) and Texas A&M University Health Science Center (TAMHSC), City of Bryan and BISD patients are able to access mental health services by direct referral. The City of Bryan and BISD pay for these services separately; however, services are incorporated as an exhibit to the Employee Health Center Agreement. Both the City of Bryan and BISD pay for six (6) visits per patient per calendar year. This service is in addition to the six (6) visits employees and dependents are eligible for through the City's Employee Assistance Program (EAP). 

 The current Professional Services Agreement with St. Joseph Regional Health Center commenced on January 1, 2023, and expires on December 31, 2025, with the option to extend for one (1) additional two (2) year term; however, with three (3) proposed changes, a new agreement is being proposed. 
 A summary of actual costs for the past three (3) years and 2025 Year-to Date (January through September YTD) can be found in table below. Of note, actual costs have historically remained under the City Council approved amounts. 
 Year 2022 2023 2024 2025 YTD 
 COB $352,004 $354,070 $369,071 $277,585 
 BISD $350,330 $344,233 $358,619 $271,662 
 BC911 N/A $7,399 $8,844 N/A 
 Total $702,334 $705,702 $736,534 $549,247 

 The City of Bryan/BISD Employee Health Center is a well-utilized facility where employees and their covered dependents (approximately 6,578 total covered lives) are able to receive quality, affordable health care. Patients visiting the Center are not required to pay a co-payment. Services at the Center currently include primary and minor acute care along with occupational health services and minor workers' compensation illnesses and injuries (City of Bryan only). The Center currently is located in close proximity to St. Joseph Regional Health Center, radiological services, and other medical specialists. 
 A summary of visits for the past three (3) years and 2025 Year-to-Date (January through September YTD) can be found in the table below. These visits include provider and nurse visits. Nurse visits can include, but are not limited to, lab draws, injections, and routine blood pressure checks. 
 Year 2022 2023 2024 2025 YTD 
 COB 4,997 4,453 4,213 2,595 
 BISD 3,473 3,122 3,259 2,358 
 BC911 N/A 23 33 N/A 
 Total 8,470 7,598 7,505 4,953 

 The current agreement expires on December 31, 2025. City staff, along with representatives from St. Joseph Medical Group and BISD met recently to discuss continuing the partnership. Three changes are being proposed to the current agreement as outlined below:

 Change the name of St. Joseph Regional Health Center to St. Joseph Medical Group : While St. Joseph Health Center and St. Joseph Medical Group are part of the same entity and operate under the same Tax ID, the ownership and signing authority differs. St. Joseph Medical Group is the group who operationalizes the Employee Health Center services and employs the staff. 
 Decrease in price of psychiatry care offered through the TAMU Behavioral Health Services (Exhibit F) : In the current agreement, psychiatry services are billed at a rate of $300 per hour. St. Joseph Medical Group has negotiated a lower price. The new price per hour will be $200 per hour.
 Removing any reference to BC911 in the Agreement : Effective January 1, 2025, BC911 no longer receives services through the Center, due to a change in insurance plans/structure for BC911.

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends approving the proposed three (3) year Professional Services Agreement in the amount of $796,631 in year one (1) with a possible 2.6% increase in subsequent years based on appropriated funds with the option to renew for an additional two (2) years with St. Joseph Medical Group to manage and operate the City of Bryan/BISD Employee Health Center. 

 Since the Professional Services Agreement is between the City and St. Joseph Health Medical Group, the City is responsible for payment of all costs associated with the agreement. However, Bryan Independent School District is invoiced by the City as specified in an Interlocal Agreement. 

 Options: 
 Approve the three (3) year Professional Services Agreement with the option to renew for an additional two (2) years with St. Joseph Medical Group to manage and operate the City of Bryan/BISD Employee Health Center.
 Make amendments to the proposed Professional Services Agreement with St. Joseph Medical Group and then approve, which may require consideration at a future City Council Meeting and additional negotiations with St. Joseph Medical Group and BISD. 
 Do not approve the proposed Professional Services Agreement, which will result in the Employee Health Center no longer being available to the City of Bryan or BISD.

 Attachments: 
 A. Proposed Professional Services Agreement with St. Joseph Medical Group
 B. Interlocal Agreement (City of Bryan & BISD) - for reference purposes and not being considered as part of this Council Action Form

 Goals 

 Infrastructure

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan and Bryan Commerce and Development (BCD) have the unique opportunity to facilitate, through the existing Bryan/Traditions Partnership, the construction of a 200-space parking garage, infrastructure, and site work to support future office, retail, restaurant, and entertainment in the master planned Lake Walk community. 

 BCD currently owns eighty percent (80%) of the limited partnership interests responsible for developing lots within the partnership in preparation of their sale and vertical development. William Cole Ventures owns the remaining twenty percent (20%). These development expenses typically include infrastructure, landscaping, and shared parking. These development expenses are split based on the ownership percentage. In turn, BCD then receives a portion of the land sale proceeds to cover these development expenditures. 

 The immediate goal is to complete the site work and parking garage to facilitate the construction of a 100,000 square foot office building and restaurant space known as The Lumin. Following The Lumin will be an entertainment venue and other commercial development around the Lake Walk development. At full build-out, this investment is anticipated to result in an excess of $20,000,000 in land sales revenue to BCD. 

 In addition, The Lumin, entertainment venue and remaining development in Lake Walk will generate significant property tax and sales tax revenue. The Lumin and entertainment venue will result in $22,000,000 (including the parking garage) and $4,600,000, respectively, in ad valorem. The remaining multi-family, entertainment, commercial, and hospitality uses are expected to result in an additional $80,000,000 in ad valorem at full build-out. 

 The site work required of Bryan/Traditions is currently estimated at $4,723,583. Completion of this infrastructure, landscaping, lighting, etc. will require a cash contribution by BCD, formalized by a Resolution approved by BCD, in an amount not to exceed $3,778,366. The lot sale associated with The Lumin alone will generate a distribution to BCD of $1,592,800. BCD also will provide a loan to William Cole for a portion of their twenty percent (20%) of the $4,723,583 in site work expenses to be paid back from future lot sales distributions. William Cole will re-pay BCD from their portion of lots sales proceeds the principal amount plus interest at the set annual interest rate. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Taking this action strengthens both the Bryan/Traditions Partnership of which BCD is a partner and the City of Bryan by enabling the construction new commercial spaces in Bryan, and thereby increasing the value of partnership land and increasing employment commerce and tax revenue for the City. For these reasons, staff recommends approval of this proposed Resolution.

 Subject 
 B. Approval of the proposed Contract with May Recreation Equipment & Design, L.P. for the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment for Villa West Park in the amount of $376,224 
 Type

 Fiscal Impact

 Budget Source 
 Parkland Dedication Funding (Single Member District 5) 
 Goals 

 Infrastructure 

 Public Safety 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 Villa West Park currently features two (2) composite play unit structures. Both play units have been internally inspected by City staff certified in playground safety, and while an immediate hazard to users does not exist, City staff recommends proceeding with replacement of the deteriorating equipment. 

 Installed circa 2000, the playground equipment located within Villa West Park has surpassed its life expectancy and has become the oldest City-owned play equipment in Single Member District 5. This park is heavily used by citizens and visitors throughout the year, resulting in the excessive use of play elements, inevitably promoting deterioration during the last twenty-five-year span. Several replacement parts have become obsolete, thus making any future equipment failures to require specific amenities within the composite structure to be taken out of service. 

 The current fall surfacing for both play units consists of a combination of poured in place (PIP) rubber at the entry points and loose fill engineered wood fiber (EWF) mulch throughout the remaining square footage. The proposed installation includes a single, unitary material consisting of bonded shredded rubber (BSR) mulch surfacing. This product will improve accessibility to the equipment and maneuverability throughout both play spaces. The proposed installation also features updated shade structures to provide favorable play conditions and increase the life expectancy of the proposed playground equipment. Included in the scope of work is the demolition and removal of the existing play units, shade structures, and surfacing. 

 May Recreation Equipment & Design, L.P. is the selected vendor for the turnkey project, inclusive of removing the existing structures, providing the new units, and complete installation. The selection was based on prior success the City has had with the vendor and the proposal’s effective use of space, the high value of the equipment, and its provision for completely upgrading fall surfaces as desired to optimally meet industry standards, while preserving the amount of shade provided over the main equipment structures. Additionally, May Recreation Equipment and Design, L.P. has gone through a competitive bid process for the parks and recreation equipment, products, and installation services as they are a contracted BuyBoard Purchasing Cooperative vendor. 

 With the replacement of these two play structures, the risk of injury will be minimized and replacement parts will be more readily available to maintain functionality as designed. The new equipment will be more aesthetically pleasing to park goers, which in turn, will improve the park system’s infrastructure along with an enhanced quality of life for the community. 

 The cost for equipment and installation will utilize Parkland Dedication funding from Single Member District 5. As of September 5, 2025, the current Parkland Dedication account balance for Single Member District 5 is $659,568.35. Parkland Dedication funds have restricted uses and enhancing park playgrounds is an acceptable use. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 During the August 19, 2025, Parks and Recreation Advisory Board meeting, a presentation for the equipment replacement, which included renderings for both play areas, was provided. The Board recommended replacing the playground equipment at Villa West Park with the proposed equipment from May Recreation & Design, L.P. 

 The Parks and Recreation Advisory Board and City staff recommend the City Council approve a contract with May Recreation & Design, L.P. for the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment for Villa West Park in the amount of $376,224. 

 Options: 
 1) Approve the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment for Villa West Park from May Recreation & Design, L.P. in the amount of $376,224. 
 2) Do not approve the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment, and provide staff direction

matters.title: G. Approval of a Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement between the City of Bryan, Bryan Commerce and Development, Inc., and the BioCorridor Property Owners Association, for the construction of a parking garage in Lake Walk in Bryan, Texas

 Subject 
 G. Approval of a Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement between the City of Bryan, Bryan Commerce and Development, Inc., and the BioCorridor Property Owners Association, for the construction of a parking garage in Lake Walk in Bryan, Texas 
 Type

 Bryan Commerce and Development fund and revenues generated from land sales in Lake Walk 
 Goals 

 Quality of Life

 Economic Development 

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan and Bryan Commerce and Development (BCD) have the unique opportunity to facilitate, through the existing Bryan/Traditions Partnership, the construction of a 200-space parking garage, infrastructure, and site work to support future office, retail, restaurant, and entertainment in the master planned Lake Walk community. 

 BCD currently owns eighty percent (80%) of the limited partnership interests responsible for developing lots within the partnership in preparation of their sale and vertical development. William Cole Ventures owns the remaining twenty percent (20%). These development expenses typically include infrastructure, landscaping, and shared parking. These development expenses are split based on the ownership percentage. In turn, BCD then receives a portion of the land sale proceeds to cover these development expenditures. 

 The proposed 200 space parking garage will be owned by the BioCorridor Property Owners Association (BPOA). The garage will be utilized by The Lumin and other developments in Lake Walk, and operations and maintenance will be funded by assessments paid by the property owners to the BPOA. This Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement, in which both BCD and the City of Bryan will be party to, memorializes the required number of parking spaces, minimum design standards, and construction timeline in exchange for financially guaranteeing the construction loan for the garage currently estimated at $1,800,000. Should any grants be made from BCD to the BPOA for this purpose, BCD will be paid a preferred return on the grant consisting of five percent (5%) on an annualized pro rata basis of the amount of any grant payments made to the Developer by BCD in addition to a guarantor fee of two percent (2%) of the total loan amount. 

 The immediate goal is to complete the site work and parking garage to facilitate the construction of a 100,000 square foot office building and restaurant space known as The Lumin. Following The Lumin will be an entertainment venue and other commercial development around the Lake Walk development. At full build-out, this investment is anticipated to result in an excess of $20,000,000 in land sales revenue to BCD. 

 In addition, The Lumin, entertainment venue and remaining development in Lake Walk will generate significant property tax and sales tax revenue. The Lumin and entertainment venue will result in $22,000,000 (including the parking garage) and $4,600,000, respectively, in ad valorem. The remaining multi-family, entertainment, commercial, and hospitality uses are expected to result in an additional $80,000,000 in ad valorem at full build-out. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Taking this action strengthens both the Bryan/Traditions Partnership of which BCD is a partner and the City of Bryan by enabling the construction new commercial spaces in Bryan, and thereby increasing the value of partnership land and increasing employment commerce and tax revenue for the City. For these reasons, staff recommends approval of this proposed Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement by Resolution
2. Provide direction to modify the Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement and reschedule it for a future City Council meeting
3. Deny the Chapter 380 Economic Development Agreement and provide direction to staff

 2. Lake Walk Illustrative Master Plan 
 3. Parking Garage Plans

 Type

 Summary: 
 The Riverside Wastewater Treatment Plant is a small service territory located north of Leonard Road across from the Brazos County Expo complex. In general, the service territory is from Leonard Road on the south, SH47 to the west, Linda Lane to the north, and Higgs Lane on the east. The City of Bryan is the water purveyor for this service area. Effective April 8, 2025, Lisa Marie Ramirez became the new owner and operator of the treatment plant and has filed paperwork with the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to establish West Bryan Wastewater, LLC as the new alternative name for the treatment plant. 

 A disconnection agreement for unpaid sewer charges was established with the previous owner of the treatment plant, Syed Hyder. A new agreement with Ms. Ramirez is needed if the City choses to continue disconnecting water service for unpaid sewer charges to West Bryan Wastewater, LLC. 

 Texas Water Code § 13.250(b)(2) empowers the holder of a water supply Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) to discontinue service for nonpayment of charges for sewer service provided by another retail public utility under an agreement between the retail public utility and the sewer CCN holder. 16 Texas Administrative Code § 24.167(e) provides that where sewer service is provided by one retail public utility and water service is provided by another retail public utility, the retail public utility that provides the water service shall disconnect water service to a customer who has not paid undisputed sewer charges, if requested by the sewer service provider and if an agreement exists between the two retail public utilities regarding such disconnection. 

 This agreement outlines the mechanism by which this agreement will be implemented. The agreement provides for notification requirements, payment requirements from West Bryan Wastewater, LLC to the City of Bryan to execute the water disconnects, and the timeframe for which notice to the customer and the City shall be provided. The payment to the City of Bryan shall be before any cutoffs are performed. The amount of the disconnection fee paid to the City of Bryan is $50 per meter, which is the maximum allowed by State statute. The City of Bryan has stated in this agreement no water customer will be disconnected from water, if there is a health and safety concern evidenced by a medical professional. There is no separate fee for the restoration of service. 

 This agreement shall be in effect for a period not to exceed five (5) years. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends the City Council approve this agreement to disconnect water service between West Bryan Wastewater, LLC and the City. Based on the terms of the agreement, the notification process should allow the City to disconnect a group of meters within one trip, instead of making multiple trips to disconnect small numbers of meters. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the proposed agreement 
 2. Do not approve the proposed agreement and provide direction

 Summary: 
 On September 9, 2025, the City Council authorized a contract for professional services for the purposes of developing a new Comprehensive Plan for the City of Bryan with Halff Associates, Inc. (“Halff”). This project relies on a high degree of public participation. Local elected and appointed officials, residents, businesses, agencies, and organizations are strongly encouraged to participate throughout the 15-month long planning process, so Halff can channel public input into feasible plan goals and objectives. The consultant team will work in partnership with a Comprehensive Plan Advisory Committee (CPAC), appointed by the City Council, to assist in the development of the plan, and to help ensure stakeholders and community residents can be involved in the planning process. 

 The CPAC will meet at least five (5) times throughout the project, either in person or through virtual meetings. Meetings are tentatively planned for October and December 2025, as well as March, May, and September 2026. Meetings are expected to be two to three hours long and are intended to provide key input, strategic direction, and general oversight of the development of the plan. The CPAC also will be invited to attend the community-wide meetings to serve as ambassadors for the planning process and the draft plan. Adoption of the plan by the City Council, anticipated for early 2027, will complete the project and the citizen volunteers’ commitment to the CPAC.

 Staff Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends the City Council appoint a CPAC (see attached list of recommended members) to receive valuable input from various groups and individuals in the community throughout this master planning process. 

 Utilizing a CPAC in this comprehensive planning effort is a proven format for obtaining stakeholder input on a wide range of interconnecting issues affecting Bryan, and promotes joint ownership of a vision for the future of Bryan. 
 The CPAC will not be the sole source of public input for the Comprehensive Plan project. The CPAC will function as a “sounding board” for the consultants during the preparation of the Comprehensive Plan Update. 
 The project’s public engagement strategy also includes focus group meetings, as well as a public survey and public workshop meeting, to help ensure broad participation from residents, community groups, and stakeholders.

 Options: 
 approve the appointment of the proposed individuals to serve on the CPAC; 
 approve the appointment of additional and or different individuals to serve on the CPAC, which may require rescheduling the request for consideration on a future City Council meeting agenda; or 
 do not approve the appointment of individual to the CPAC at this time and provide direction to staff.

 B. Approval of a second amendment to the contract with Digitech Computer, Inc., adding the Medicare Ground Ambulance Data Collection System (GADCS) services report preparation and submission to the existing contract for billing of Emergency Medical Services (ambulance billing services) and the Texas Ambulance Supplemental Payment Program ("TASPP") report preparation and submission for a total contract amount not to exceed $217,500 annually.

 Summary: 
 Beginning in Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, Medicare requires all ground ambulance service providers and suppliers selected to participate in the Medicare Ground Ambulance Data Collection System (GADCS) to collect and report cost, revenue, and utilization data as mandated; failure to submit the required information will result in a 10% reduction in allowable Medicare payments for ambulance services. The City contracts with Digitech to provide ambulance billing services and other reporting items. This proposed second amendment adds the additional report preparation and submission for the Medicare Ground Ambulance Data Collection System (GADCS) services for a total contract amount not to exceed $217,500 annually. The fee for the report preparation and submission for the GADCS services will be $17,500. 

 Other minor revisions included in the amendment involve relocating certain contract language to the appropriate sections and implementing an increase in the credit inquiry rate—from $0.11 to $0.55 per valid transaction record submitted—due to changes in the credit program. This adjustment is expected to result in an approximate annual cost increase of $900 for this service and will generate a higher return through the TASPP reporting.

 The proposed second amendment to the contract for the billing of Emergency Medical Services ("EMS", or ambulance billing services) with Digitech Computer, Inc (“Digitech”) includes the Texas Ambulance Supplemental Payment Program ("TASPP") and the Medicare Ground Ambulance Data Collection System (GADCS) services report preparation and submission for a total contract amount not to exceed $217,500 annually, for the term of the contract. Digitech’s fee for ambulance billing and TASPP preparation will be 4.95% of net revenue collected for each service and t he fee for the report preparation and submission for the GADCS services will be $17,500. The term of this contract will run from October 15, 2025, through November 30, 2026. 

 Digitech will provide for continued ambulance billing services for the City of Bryan Emergency Medical Services as a sole source provider. Digitech is a leader in the industry with proprietary software (designed, updated, and maintained in house) and policies and procedures that consistently allow the City to recover costs of providing ambulance services. Further, Digitech’s customer service to City staff, citizens, and patients is exemplary. Digitech has proactively helped the City design a payment plan program and redesigned the City's invoices to be more transparent and useful for patients, all at no charge to the City. Digitech also will provide report preparation and submission, as well as audit support for the Texas Ambulance Supplemental Payment Program ("TASPP"). 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Digitech has performed this service for the City of Bryan for the past fourteen (14) years. They have consistently provided a proactive approach to short-paid accounts, working with the City to provide different billing and payment options, and also provided administration of the City's Ambulance Charity Care Program. 

 A five-year history of the fees paid to Digitech are listed below: 

 -2021: $133,648 
 -2022: $139,604 
 -2023: $169,749 
 -2024: $146,003 
 -2025: $180,200 

 Staff recommends amending this contract by approving the proposed second amendment with Digitech. 

 Options: 
 Approve the contract amendment with Digitech at a rate of $17,500 for GADCS services and $0.55 per valid transaction inquiry record submitted . 
 Do not approve the contract amendment with Digitech (which will result in a disruption of ambulance billing services) and provide direction to staff.

 Summary: 
 A Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Annual Contract for Parks Custodial Services was issued on October 24, 2023. Sealed proposals were submitted to the Purchasing Department on November 16, 2023. The City received responses from four (4) vendors. These vendors included Garcia Cleaning Service, PureService Corporation, Junction Five-0-Five, and Superior Commercial Cleaning. 

 City staff provided a thorough review of all proposals. Evaluation criteria included, but was not limited to, the overall cost proposal, references, relevant experience, and familiarity with the City of Bryan. City staff recommended to City Council that PureService Corporation of Southlake, Texas would provide the best value for the City of Bryan. The City Council approved the recommendation to proceed with the contract award at the December 12, 2023 meeting. The first one-year extension was recommended to and approved by the City Council at the December 10, 2024 meeting. 

 The initial term of this contract was one (1) year with four (4) additional one-year extension options pending approval by the City Council for a possible total of five (5) years. Monthly pressure-washing of pavilion and restroom areas is required. The contractor also is responsible for pre- and post-cleanings of rented facilities that fall outside of scheduled service visits.

 After evaluation of overall job performance during the second term of this contract, staff determined PureService Corporation met or exceeded all contract terms. The contractor consistently provided a quality service/product, addressed identified deficiencies in a timely manner, and has a dedicated management team that takes pride in their service.  Summary: 
 In 2016, the City Council adopted the City of Bryan Financial Management Policy Statements (FMPS). These statements were designed to assemble the City’s major financial policies into one document. The statements are a tool used to ensure the City is financially able to meet its current and future service needs. 
 The stated objectives of the FMPS are: 
 To guide the City Council and management policy decisions that have significant fiscal impact. 
 To employ balanced revenue policies that provide adequate funding for services and service levels. 
 To maintain appropriate financial capacity for present and future needs. 
 To maintain sufficient reserves to maintain service levels during periods of economic downturn. 
 To promote sound financial management by providing accurate and timely information on the City’s financial condition. 
 To protect the City’s credit rating and provide for adequate resources to meet the provisions of the City’s debt obligations on all municipal debt. 
 To ensure the legal use of financial resources through an effective system of internal controls. 
 To enhance transparency in financial matters. 
 Included in the FMPS is a biennial requirement to review and update, if needed, any of the FMPS to better reflect statutory requirements or any change in policy. 
 In January 2018, the City Council amended the FMPS updating reporting requirements as well as the required and target ending balances for specific funds. The amendment also included several housekeeping items intended to make the document easier to read (e.g., formatting, clarification, etc.). 
 In January 2020, the City Council amended the FMPS updating several items with regard to the approval and selection of the City's external auditor, lien collection practices, target unrestricted cash for various funds, and specific debt coverage matrices for BTU City and Rural. 
 In September 2020, the City Council amended the FMPS updating the sections on Debt Financing, Debt Structures, and Use of Debt Financing to accommodate the issuance and debt schedules of the City's General Obligation Pension Bonds, Series 2020. This amendment also included several housekeeping items intended to clarify the intent of certain sections of the document. 
 In November 2021, the City Council amended the FMPS updating target unrestricted cash for BTU City, BTU Rural, and the Employee Benefits Fund. This amendment also included several housekeeping items intended to clarify the intent of certain sections of the document. 
 In October 2024, the City Council amended the FMPS updating the capitalization threshold from $5,000 to $10,000 along with adjusting wording for clarification and terminology updates. 
 Staff recommends the following changes to the City's FMPS: 
 Sections: II.D – Updated Financial Advisory Services contract duration to reflect the evergreen term with a termination clause. 
 Section: VI.D – Updated reference from Unassigned to Unrestricted for the General Fund Balance to align with best practice. 
 Section: VI.I – Established the target fund balance for the Self-Insurance Fund to be the greater of $2.5 million or the stop-loss deductible, which ensures the balance target is at least $2.5 million. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 At the October 21, 2025, Audit Committee meeting, the Audit Committee unanimously recommended approving the Policy amendments. Staff also recommends approving the changes outlined above. 

 Options: 
 Adopt policy amendments as proposed 
 Adopt a portion of the policy amendments as proposed, which may require consideration at a future City Council meeting 
 Do not adopt the policy amendments as proposed and provide direction to staff

 Summary: 
 The City of Bryan has several water and sewer lines located within the limits of the State Highway (SH) 6 widening project. Some lines conflict with proposed Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) improvements and others need to be upgraded due to size and/or condition. This proposed construction contract involves replacing three (3) existing sanitary sewer lines and one (1) water line. 

 One of the sanitary sewer lines is just south of the Old Reliance/East Martin Luther King, Jr. Street bridge. This 18-inch sewer line is undersized and has condition issues.  Once the new lines are installed, the existing lines will be removed or grout filled.

 Summary: 
 Over the last couple of years, the City of Bryan and RELLIS leadership have had discussions on the City of Bryan treating the wastewater from the RELLS Campus. The City of Bryan is currently installing a gravity line, lift station, and force main west of SH47. This $19 million investment makes sewer service to the RELLIS Campus a possibility. 

 The proposed interlocal agreement between Texas A&M University System and the City of Bryan outlines the wastewater rate that RELLIS will pay for service. This rate is the same as the commercial/industrial rate for users inside the City. The RELLIS Campus also will be subject to the City's Industrial Pretreatment Program and associated surcharges as outlined by City ordinances. Lastly, the interlocal agreement puts a limit on the volume of wastewater the RELLIS Campus can send to the City of Bryan for treatment. This volume limit is 225,000 gallons per day and represents 11.25% of the Thompsons Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant's (WWTP) capacity. 

 Texas A&M University System will own all of the infrastructure located within their campus including any pump station or piping needed to connect to the City's existing project. 

 Should the RELLIS Campus need additional capacity above the 225,000 gallons, a provision within the agreement provides for discussion between the two parties on financial contributions to the capital costs of expanding the Thompsons Creek WWTP. 

 Staff recommends the City Council approve the proposed interlocal agreement between the City of Bryan and Texas A&M University System for the sewer service to the RELLIS Campus.

matters.text:
Agenda Item Details

 Goals 

 Public Safety 

 Quality of Life 

 Infrastructure 

 Summary: 
 This purchase is for the replacement of the Public Safety Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system for the Bryan Fire Department, Bryan Police Department, Brazos County Sheriff's Office, Brazos County Volunteer Fire Departments, Brazos County Constable agencies, and the Brazos County 911 District. 

 The current system, purchased and implemented in 2003-2004, has not kept pace with technological advancements. The existing Tiburon Total Command CAD product, acquired by Tritech Technology in 2015 and subsequently by CentralSquare Technology (CST) in 2018, is no longer sold to new customers, is not being further developed, and receives limited vendor support. Furthermore, the Tiburon Total Command system does not offer the same level of interagency operability or advanced automated features as the CentralSquare Technology Enterprise CAD, particularly in real-time data sharing and multi-agency coordination. 

 This Council Action Form is for the purchase of a five-year Services Agreement for the CentralSquare Enterprise CAD software system project and ongoing support, totaling $1,304,606.00 for the contract, with the City of Bryan's amount being $774,929.80 after deducting reimbursements from Brazos County and the emergency services districts (ESD) reimbursements. 

 The total City of Bryan cost amount for each year is below: 
 Year 1 - $202,807.13 
 Year 2 - $191,036.51 
 Year 3 - $127,028.72 
 Year 4 - $127,028.72 
 Year 5 - $127,028.72 
 Total - $774,929.80 

 The total contract cost amount for each year is below: 
 Year 1 - $340,623.15 
 Year 2 - $321,005.45 
 Year 3 - $214,325.80 
 Year 4 - $214,325.80 
 Year 5 - $214,325.80 
 Total - $1,304,606 

 The total reimbursement amount from Brazos County and the four (4) ESDs: 
 Year 1 - $137,816.02 
 Year 2 - $129,968.94 
 Year 3 - $87,297.08 
 Year 4 - $87,297.08 
 Year 5 - $87,297.08 
 Total - $529,676.20 

 This purchase directly supports the mission of the public safety departments by enabling increased services to the citizens of Bryan, in coordination with Brazos County and the Brazos County 911 District. Specifically, CentralSquare's CAD system can be configured to identify calls that may not require traditional emergency responses. By triaging calls based on caller information, previous call history, and potentially other integrated data sources, the system can identify opportunities for alternative response strategies. 

 For example, if a caller frequently contacts 911 for non-emergency medical assistance, the CAD system can flag these calls for dispatching community paramedics instead of fire engines and ambulances. This capability will help identify non-emergency calls that can be diverted to the on-duty community paramedic, reducing call volume for ambulance and fire crews while providing more appropriate care in a suitable setting. 

 This approach can potentially improve patient outcomes and satisfaction. Furthermore, Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) and community paramedic programs can be integrated into the CAD system to ensure proper follow-up, and data from these visits can be fed back into the system, enhancing the accuracy of future call screenings and responses. 

 Other users of this software in the state of Texas include College Station, Plano, Austin, and current contract negotiations in place with Texas A&M University Police Department. The Enterprise CAD software appears to be the best solution for the City of Bryan to assist with managing Public Safety dispatching and offers improved transparency of the process. 

 CentralSquare is a member of The Interlocal Purchasing System (TIPS) with Contract number 220105. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Approval of the purchase of Public Safety Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) software for the City of Bryan contract for the not to exceed amount of $1,304,606.00 consisting of first year and implementation cost of $340,623.15, second year and implementation cost of $321,005.45, and annual fees amounting to $214,325.80/year for Years 3 - 5. 

 After reimbursements from Brazos County and the Brazos County Volunteer Fire Departments, costs for the City of Bryan for the not to exceed amount of $774,929.80 consisting of first year and implementation cost of $202,807.13, second year and implementation cost of $191,036.51, and annual fees amounting to $127,028.72/year for Years 3 - 5. 

 Staff recommends approval of the purchase of the CentralSquare software platform to assist with dispatching Public Safety for the City of Bryan to increase efficiency, minimize error, provide ease of access to data, improve transparency, improve inter-departmental coordination, and satisfy auditing concerns. 

 Options: 
 Approve the proposed Solutions Agreement with CentralSquare for the Enterprise CAD software including setup and support of the software. 
 Do not approve and provide direction to staff. 

 Attachments: 
 Proposed Solutions Agreement with CentralSquare Technologies, LLC

Participating agencies include the City of Bryan, Brazos County, and Emergency Service Districts (ESD) 1, 2, 3, and 4. 

 The City of Bryan and regional partners are replacing the legacy Tiburon/Tritech CAD (originally implemented in 2003–2004) with CentralSquare’s Enterprise CAD to improve interagency operability, real-time data sharing, and multi-agency coordination. The legacy product is no longer sold, receives limited vendor support, and lacks modern automation features. Reimbursements from Brazos County and the ESDs reduce the City of Bryan’s share consistent with the cost schedule outlined in the Enterprise CAD Council Action Form (on this same City Council agenda). 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation:

The ILA also authorizes the Mayor to execute related documents, and defines term, renewal/termination. Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 H. Approval of a Contract with Team Solutions, LLC for the replacement of Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers at the Bryan Justice Center and Bryan Municipal Office Building in the total amount of $192,012. 
 Type 
 Action (Statutory) 
 Preferred Date 
 Jan 13, 2026

 Jan 13, 2026

 192,012.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source

 Goals 

 Infrastructure 

 Service 

 Summary: 
 Currently, the Bryan Municipal Office Building and the Bryan Justice Center are equipped with Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers that allow for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) components to communicate with one another to manage overall climate control. The existing controllers are supported by a Local Operation Network (LON), and while still operational, these units are slowly becoming obsolete with replacement parts becoming more difficult to acquire. The existing controllers have met their life expectancy and the need for replacements has begun due to on-going equipment failures. 

 Modern systems are transitioning to equipment with Building Automation and Control Network (BACnet) capabilities, allowing for more centralized control, while improving overall efficiency. This proposed contract provides for the replacement of the existing VAV controllers with Delta controllers at both facilities. Delta Controls, an industry-leading manufacturer of building control systems, allows for future compatibility with large scale equipment (i.e., rooftop units, boilers, makeup air units, etc.) regardless of manufacturer. 

 Bryan Municipal Office Building: The contract scope includes replacing a total of forty (40) Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers with new Delta controllers. The original controllers (installed circa 1987) were replaced in May 2006 during HVAC upgrades. The scope of work includes the following: new communication wiring, new Fan Power Terminal boxes (FPT), replacing VAV controllers with new Delta controllers, new thermostats, new Discharge Air Temperature (DAT) sensors, and all required programming, updated graphics, and verification of proper operation. This portion of the contract totals $66,759. 

 Bryan Justice Center: The contract scope includes replacing a total of seventy-seven (77) Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers with Delta controllers. The original Building Automation System (BAS) and controllers were installed and commissioned in June of 2008. The scope of work includes the following: new communication wiring, new Fan Power Terminal boxes (FPT), replacing VAV controllers with new Delta controllers, new thermostats, new Discharge Air Temperature (DAT) sensors, and all required programming, updated graphics, and verification of proper operation. This portion of the contract totals $125,253. 

 Funding for the proposed contract has been budgeted through an approved Decision Package (DP) for Fiscal Year 2026. The DP is in the amount of $136,000, and is for the Justice Center. The remaining balance of the DP will be applied to the Municipal Office Building with the remaining funding for that project being from the Facility Improvement Plan (FIP), and was budgeted at $73,000 for Fiscal Year 2026. 

 Team Solutions, LLC is a contracted vendor through Buy Board, a purchasing cooperative in which contracts are competitively solicited and publicly awarded. 

 With the assistance from a third-party consultant, staff anticipates receiving an Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant (EECBG) to allow for partial or full reimbursement for replacement of the equipment identified in the proposed contract scope. Pre-approval grant funding has been received from the Department of Energy. Staff will be required to provide supporting evidence of equipment replacements throughout the process and after all requirements are met, grant funding is to be released. At this time, the EECBG reimbursement amount is estimated at $140,860. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 With existing equipment meeting life expectancy and multiple controllers no longer functioning as designed, staff recommends the City Council approve a contract with Team Solutions, LLC for the replacement of Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers at the Bryan Justice Center and Bryan Municipal Building in the total amount of $192,012. 

 Options: 
 1) Approve the proposed contract with Team Solutions, LLC for the replacement of Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers at the Bryan Justice Center and Bryan Municipal Office Building in the total amount of $192,012. 

 2) Do not approve the proposed contract with Team Solutions, LLC for the replacement of Variable Air Volume (VAV) controllers at the Bryan Justice Center and Bryan Municipal Office Building in the total amount of $192,012 and provide staff with direction.

 Summary: 
 In 2008, BTU and Water Services entered into an agreement with R.W. Beck to develop a business case for an Advanced Meter Infrastructure (AMI) system. In 2009, results of the business case were presented to the City Council, as staff asked permission to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to possible AMI vendors. After receiving City Council direction, staff received three proposals from AMI system vendors. After evaluating the proposals, staff selected Sensus as the preferred vendor. In early 2010, staff asked the City Council for permission to negotiate with Sensus on a contract for the installation of the AMI system. On February 22, 2011, the City Council approved a contract with Sensus for the development, procurement, and implementation of the AMI system. 

 Although the system is fully functional, growth and maintenance expenses are ongoing. With several new development projects underway, another year of elevated service connections is expected. A typical residential water connection costs approximately $200 for the meter and communication module, and consequently, staff anticipates spending approximately $200,000 to manage growth rates. Staff also provides for a one percent (1%) failure rate of infrastructure over the entire system. While many of these components will be replaced under warranty, if they fail, the return merchandise authorization (RMA) process takes time. The remaining $50,000 allows for surplus inventory to be readily available to replace items not covered under warranty and to mitigate processing time on warranty items. These purchases qualify as sole source procurements, and a sole source letter is on file. 

 The following are historical expenses over the past eleven (11) years: 
 FY25 - $248,000.00
 FY24 - $249,993.62 
 FY23 - $249,924.40 
 FY22 - $332,162.78 
 FY21 - $249,962.27 
 FY20 - $199,914.32 
 FY19 - $149,409.41 
 FY18 - $49,951.20 
 FY17 - $205,461.90 
 FY16 - $349,953.65 
 FY15 - $1,000,413.90 

 Notes: Through Fiscal Year (FY) 2017, the prices are somewhat elevated as the existing infrastructure was still being converted to the AMI system. In FY 2018, the expense was abnormally low as stock items purchased during the conversion were pulled from inventory and installed in the system. 

 Staff recommends the City Council authorize the purchase of meters and communication modules through Sensus for the ongoing installation and expansion of an AMI system for Water Services at an amount not to exceed $250,000. This purchase order will be set up through a blanket purchase order (BPO), and funds only will be expended for meters and modules ordered. This authorization allows staff to purchase up to $250,000 worth of equipment during FY 2026. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends approving the purchase of meters and communication modules through Sensus for the ongoing installation and expansion of an Advanced Meter Infrastructure system for Water Services. AMI has the ability to reduce billing and operational costs, plus provide time of use and leak detection to customers. Revenue will be maximized by upgrading underperforming meters with more accurate meters. 

 Options: 
 1. Authorize the expenditure of funds 
 2. Modify the expenditure amount, which may require consideration at a future City Council meeting 
 3. Provide direction to staff

 Summary: 
 On October 7, 2025, City staff issued a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for architectural firms to provide the City of Bryan with professional architectural and engineering services necessary for the design and construction of an Animal Center to be located off of Martin Luther King, Jr. Street. On October 28, thirteen (13) responses were received. Staff evaluated and narrowed the field of respondents to three (3) of the highest scoring firms. 
 In an effort to determine the top overall ranked firm, staff invited representatives of the three (3) finalist firms to make oral presentations and participate in onsite interviews with City staff. As a result, staff selected Jackson & Ryan Architects of Houston, Texas as the top firm for this project. 
 The structure of the proposed Agreement has the architect contracting with the design team, inclusive of Structural, Mechanical, and Electrical Engineering. The architect provides services for Schematic Design, Design Development, Construction Documents, Procurement (Bidding/Negotiation), collaborates on cost estimates, budget adherence, and construction sequencing. For the actual construction of the Animal Center, the City will enter into a contract with a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR). Staff is planning on releasing a RFQ within thirty (30) days of the City Council approving this proposed Agreement with the architect. 
 The City of Bryan’s budget for the new Animal Center is $7,400,000. Over the years, City of Bryan Animal Services has received donations, with $397,662 being available for furniture, fixtures, and equipment (FF&E). The architects fee for services is $510,100. Additionally, $14,900 is needed for the architect's reimbursable expenses bringing the total not-to-exceed amount of $525,000 (i.e., $510,100 + $14,900). The not-to-exceed Agreement amount of $525,000 covers Jackson & Ryan’s architectural fee along with the structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) engineering. The remaining $6,875,000 will cover the CMAR’s fee and other professional services contracts the City will have for the project. Professional services contracts under the City's responsibility include: Material Testing, Geotechnical, Landscaping, and Civil Engineering. 
 Staff is prepared to move forward with the award of the proposed Agreement to secure professional architectural and engineering services necessary for the design and construction of the City’s new Animal Center. 
 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff's analysis indicates commercial construction costs are rising by over seven percent (7%) annually. With a fixed budget and an estimated cost of $600 per square foot, staff anticipates a facility size of between 10,000 and 11,000 square feet. The current facility, built in about 1980, is approximately 7,000 square feet. Moving forward promptly is advised to maximize the size of the facility within the current budget. 

 Staff recommends the City Council approved the proposed Agreement, which authorizes the Mayor to execute the contract with Jackson & Ryan Architects for a total not-to-exceed amount of $525,000. 
 O ptions: 
 Approve the Agreement with Jackson & Ryan Architects to provide the architectural and engineering services necessary for the design and construction of a new City of Bryan Animal Center. 
 Do not approve the Agreement with Jackson & Ryan Architects to provide the architectural and engineering services necessary for the design and construction of a new City of Bryan Animal Center and provide direction to staff.

matters.text:

Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject 
 B. Approval of a Contract for Request for Proposal No. 26-005 “Renovation of Fire Station No. 4” with Aggieland Construction, LTD, in an amount not to exceed $309,900. 
 Type 
 Action (Consent) 
 Preferred Date 
 Mar 10, 2026 
 Absolute Date 
 Mar 10, 2026 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 309,900.00 
 Budgeted 
 No 
 Budget Source 
 General Fund 
 Goals 

 Infrastructure 

 Public Safety 

 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 The existing heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system at City of Bryan Fire Station No. 4 has been identified as being under-sized for the space resulting in a negative pressure environment. Consequently, mold developed along duct lines due to condensation above lay in ceiling spaces. In preparation for construction activities to be coordinated to address the inefficient mechanical system, a required asbestos survey prior to construction activities identified elevated concentrations within mastic adhesive on the underside of floor tiling throughout the facility. 

 Following the mitigation of mold and asbestos abatement services, renovations are necessary to allow the facility to be occupied by Fire Department personnel. The facility’s apparatus bay is not affected by mitigation activities and remains operational. The Fire Department personnel have relocated to temporary housing adjacent to the facility allowing them to remain on location. 

 Staff contracted with local mechanical and architectural firms to provide construction documents for the required renovations. The scope of work consists of complete replacement of the HVAC mechanical system, new windows, spray insulation to attic spaces, new flooring throughout, electrical lighting upgrades, new lay-in and sheetrock ceilings, fresh paint, improved accessibility in restrooms, and improved accessible parking. The work also will provide climate control capabilities in the Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) storage space adjacent to the apparatus bay. Alternate pricing has been provided to upgrade the apparatus bay lighting to LED fixtures similar to the new interior installations for the City’s consideration, which will be determined as work progresses. Minor general carpentry work will be conducted by internal staff while space is unoccupied. 

 A Request for Proposal (RFP) was issued on December 9, 2025, with proposals being due January 15, 2026. S even (7) responses were received with one (1) proposal not being considered due to the vendor providing an incomplete scope of work. Evaluation criteria consisted of the proposed cost, qualifications/experience, methodology including technical approach and clear understanding of scope of work, project timeline, and vendor references. Following review by the City’s evaluation team of all proposals submitted, Aggieland Construction, LTD of College Station was determined to have provided the best value to the City. 

 The total cost to date of $83,363 is itemized below (does not include the proposed contract amount being considered with this Council Action Form): 

 Mold/Asbestos testing/third-party mitigation protocols $3,100 
 Mold Mitigation: $7,720 
 Asbestos Mitigation: $8,600 
 Temporary Housing/Associated expenses for mobilization: $27,400 
 Design Services (Architectural/Mechanical): $31,880 
 Facility Services Hourly Staff Labor (work orders): $4,663 

 The anticipated timeline for renovations to be complete once the contractor is provided with a notice to proceed is one-hundred forty (140) calendar days. Pending final date of contract execution, substantial completion is projected to be reached the first week of August 2026, dependent on weather and other factors. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 With the need to upgrade the mechanical system to address the negative pressure environment that resulted in mold development and following asbestos abatement, construction services provided at a fair market price by an experienced firm is recommended to meet the requirements of this renovation project. 

 After extensive review of all proposals submitted for this RFP, staff recommends the City Council approve the proposed contract with Aggieland Construction, LTD for Request for Proposal No. 26-005 “Renovation of Fire Station No. 4” in an amount not to exceed $309,900. 

 Options: 
 1) Approve the proposed contract with Aggieland Construction, LTD for Request for Proposal No. 26-005 “Renovation of Fire Station No. 4” in an amount not to exceed $309,900. 
 2) Do not approve the proposed contract and provide staff with direction.

 BTU’s Fleet Replacement Guide establishes that vehicles and equipment should be replaced before service delivery is impaired, using best-practice benchmarks based on age, usage (miles/hours), condition, and lifecycle cost. The bucket trucks identified for replacement meet or exceed these replacement criteria and align with BTU’s long-range fleet management philosophy. 
 The replacement of these fleet trucks has been delayed beyond the originally planned schedule due to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing supply chain constraints. In addition, manufacturers have been unable to meet the industry-wide demand for specialty utility trucks, which has extended delivery timelines. These circumstances contributed to the current timing of replacement while still adhering to BTU’s proactive fleet management strategy. 
 The bucket trucks identified for replacement are Units 21-113, 21-115, and 21-117. These vehicles are 11–12 years old, exceeding the Fleet Guide’s recommended replacement age. The units have accumulated 11,363 hours, 11,257 hours, and 10,237 hours, respectively, which significantly exceed the 6,000-hour guideline. For aerial devices, operating hours are the primary indicator of equipment wear and overall lifecycle condition. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 

 Staff recommends that the BTU Board of Directors authorize the Board Chair to authorize the purchase of three 55' Altec AA55 bucket trucks from Altec Industries, Inc. in the amount of $910,011.

 Subject 
 D. Approval of a Design Contract for Midtown North Street Reconstructions, City Job Number 332-411-425-611-DE-2512, to Schultz Engineering LLC in the not to exceed amount of $725,000.

 Goals

 Infrastructure 

 Summary: 
 This project includes the design and reconstruction of three roadway corridors within the Midtown Park North District: Bomber Drive, Williamson Drive, and West Carson Street. These roadways serve as primary access routes to Travis Bryan Midtown Park and surrounding neighborhoods but currently lack the capacity, drainage infrastructure, and multimodal features needed to support existing and future demand. The proposed improvements will upgrade roadway sections, replace aging utilities, improve drainage, and enhance pedestrian connectivity to support continued growth in the Midtown area. 

 Bomber Drive and Williamson Drive are currently narrow, approximately 20-foot-wide asphalt roadways with open ditch drainage, limited pedestrian infrastructure, and aging water systems originally installed in the 1950s. Both corridors function as key internal circulation routes, providing access to Travis Park Fields, Legends Event Center, Williamson Park Skate Park, other Midtown Park amenities, and nearby residential areas. West Carson Street serves as an east–west connection between South College Avenue and the Union Pacific Railroad and is identified as a future minor arterial and bicycle route. Existing pavement and utilities along West Carson Street are in poor condition and require full reconstruction. 

 Improvements include reconstruction of Bomber Drive from West Carson Street to Williamson Drive and Williamson Drive from South College Avenue to the Burton Creek tributary crossings. Roadways will be widened where feasible, including the addition of a center turn lane on Bomber Drive. Open ditch drainage will be replaced with curb and gutter and underground storm sewer, and water and sanitary sewer utilities will be replaced to meet current standards. 

 Multimodal improvements include construction of an 8-foot shared-use path along Bomber Drive, sidewalk connections along Williamson Drive, and potential bicycle accommodations along West Carson Street. Additional improvements include street lighting, intersection upgrades, and streetscape elements to improve safety and accessibility. 

 Portions of Williamson Drive are located within a FEMA-designated floodplain and cross Burton Creek tributaries, requiring hydrologic and hydraulic analysis and a potential Letter of Map Revision (LOMR). Similar drainage coordination may be required along West Carson Street. Utility coordination including relocation of overhead utilities by BTU will be required throughout the project. 

 This project supports the City’s long-term vision for Travis Bryan Midtown Park and aligns with the Midtown Area Plan by improving access, connectivity, and infrastructure, while supporting adjacent development. 

 Four (4) responses were received to Request For Qualifications (RFQ) #25-045 and after interviews with the top scoring firms, Schultz Engineering, LLC was found to rank the highest. 

 The Design Contract, in the amount of $725,000 or approximately 7.1% of the Engineer’s Estimate of Probable Construction Costs of $10,215,000, includes the following highlights: 

 1. Surveying / Data Collection/ Planning 
 2. Public Involvement and Outreach 
 3. Drainage and LOMR Coordination 
 4. Utility Coordination 
 5. Construction Documents and Cost Estimating Preparation 
 6. Bid Phase Services 
 7. Construction Phase Services 

 Funding for the design of these projects is Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Bonds. Currently, $400,000 of the $725,000 design cost is funded through the FY2026 Bond Funds (Fund 378), as adopted in Resolution 4163 (FY2026–2030 CIP). The remainder ($325,000) is proposed to come from the Transportation Fund. 

 Approximately $7.2 million of the estimated $10.2 million construction cost is funded through the FY2026 Bond Funds under the same CIP plans. An additional $1.8 million will be funded from the water and sewer funds. The balance of $1.2 million is proposed to come from the Transportation Fund, if the City Council supports amending the approved Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to reconstruct West Carson Street. 

 West Carson Street is included in this contract to allow for a coordinated design across all three corridors. The West Carson Street Reconstruction project (ST_09_046) has been included on the City’s CIP list since 2009 and was last estimated at approximately $2.3 million. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends approval of the Design Contract for Midtown North Street Reconstructions, City Job Number 332-411-425-611-DE-2512, to Schultz Engineering LLC in the not to exceed amount of $725,000. 

 Options: 
 1. Approve the Design Contract 
 2. Do not approve the Design Contract and provide direction to staff

 2. Midtown Park North Street Reconstruction Objective exhibit 
 3. Midtown Park North Street Reconstruction Preliminary Layout exhibit 
 4. Request for Qualification #25-045

 City staff has identified a numbering discrepancy within Chapter 62 – Land and Site Development, and two incorrect cross-references within Chapter 130 – Zoning.  In Section 130-33(g)(2), the current reference for Conditional Use Permit requests within a Historic Preservation Overlay District incorrectly cites Section 130-24, which pertains to the Innovation Corridor – Research and Development District (IC-RS), adopted in October 2022 (Ordinance No. 2586).  All proposed corrections are administrative in nature, are straightforward to implement, and do not alter or impact the substantive requirements of the ordinance.

 Summary: 
 BTU staff have developed a revised BTU Electric Rate Ordinance that provides more appropriate terminology for rate components, more natural customer class names, summarized rate tables, and easier document navigation. These changes are designed to help improve customer understanding of BTU rate structures by providing better clarity and transparency. The revised Electric Rate Ordinance eliminates seasonal rates for residential customers by replacing the seasonal component with an annual average. To summarize, the proposed Ordinance: 
 reduces duplicative language; 
 streamlines the structure; 
 simplifies terminology; and 
 eliminates seasonal rates beginning November 1, 2026. 

 This revised BTU Electric Rate Ordinance does not include modifications to "Base" rates for any customer class; the revisions are designed to be more easily understandable for customers. To note, the BTU Base Rate has not changed since 2018. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 The proposed revised Electric Rate Ordinance includes terms of service, a definition section (currently does not exist), a consolidation of rates, (e.g., City and Rural residential on a single chart), and combined rate components. The BTU Board of Directors approved modifications to the Power Cost Recovery Charge and the Transmission Cost Recovery Charge components of customer rates at their April meeting. Based on these modifications and the elimination of seasonal rates to a single rate throughout the year, an average residential customer (1000 kWh/month) will see an average increase of $3.94/month. This change is an overall increase of 3.5% to an average residential customer’s bill, which is significantly lower than the rate of inflation (i.e., 28%) since BTU’s last “base” rate change in 2018. 

 The BTU Board of Directors unanimously approved a recommendation to the City Council to approve the revised Electric Rate Ordinance, with an effective date of June 1, 2026. S taff also recommends the City Council approve the proposed revised Electric Rate Ordinance.

 Subject 
 I. Consideration of a Contract Agreement for Request for Qualifications (RFQ) No. 26-015 “Design/Build Services for the Replacement of Existing HVAC System for City of Bryan Fire Station No. 2” with SpawGlass Construction Corp. in an amount not to exceed $1,450,000 
 Type

 Apr 14, 2026 
 Absolute Date 
 Apr 14, 2026 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 1,450,000.00 
 Budgeted 
 No 
 Budget Source 
 General Fund 

 Summary: 
 Construction of City of Bryan Fire Station No. 2 began in 2016 and was occupied by Fire Department personnel in September 2018. The Fire Station requires replacement of its heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system due to the failure of the original LG Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) system installed during construction of the facility. The Fire Station is currently operating using temporary equipment consisting of a 25-ton portable HVAC unit powered by a 100-kW diesel generator to maintain climate control and allow uninterrupted Fire Department operations. 

 The exact cause of the system’s premature failure has not been definitively identified. Possible contributing factors include early system activation during construction, manufacturing defects, design or installation issues, the complexity and sensitivity of VRF systems, or a combination of these factors. While minor issues were initially resolved through service repairs and warranty replacements, failures became more frequent and severe over time. Despite involvement from multiple vendors and consultants, a long-term solution was never identified, and the system ultimately failed in October 2024. 

 Since the Fire Station opened, the HVAC system has experienced repeated coil leaks, compressor failures, and refrigerant loss. Temporary cooling equipment was first deployed in June 2021. Multiple repair attempts, including replacing evaporator coils with coated units and engaging certified LG service providers, were unsuccessful in resolving the ongoing issues. 

 From April 2019 to present, the City has spent $459,093 on HVAC-related expenses, including repairs, replacement parts, service contracts, temporary cooling equipment, and generator fuel. Additionally, City staff attempted to work with the original architect and contractor to address problems, but ultimately after consulting with external legal and subject matter experts, staff recognized a replacement system is the best option to resolve ongoing problems. 

 To address the issue permanently, the City issued Request of Qualifications (RFQ) No. 26-015 for design-build services to replace the existing HVAC system. Four (4) firms submitted qualifications: R.E.C. Industries, Inc., SpawGlass Construction Corp., E3 Entegral Solutions, Inc., and PATH Company, LLC. Based on evaluation criteria including qualifications, experience, project approach, and references, SpawGlass Construction Corp. of College Station was determined to provide the best value to the City. 

 The proposed project includes design and installation of a new Direct Expansion (DX) split HVAC system to replace the existing VRF system. The system will feature non-proprietary components that are widely available, improved redundancy so failure of one unit will not impact the entire facility, gas-fired furnaces to reduce electrical demand, and two Dedicated Outdoor Air System (DOAS) units to improve ventilation and air conditioning efficiency. The project will also include demolition of the existing system, necessary plumbing and electrical modifications, installation of exterior equipment pads, and restoration of any building finishes affected by construction. 

 The anticipated Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the project is $1,450,000, including $155,137 in pre-construction services and a construction phase fee of $125,304. Following completion of the design and bid proposal stage, the final GMP will be confirmed and presented to the City for acceptance. If approved, the project is anticipated to reach substantial completion by July 2027, assuming a Notice to Proceed is issued by August 28, 2026. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 After multiple repair attempts and consultant evaluations failed to identify a reliable long-term solution, staff recommends approval of the design-build agreement with SpawGlass Construction Corp. to replace the HVAC system at City of Bryan Fire Station No. 2. 

 Options: 
 Approve the proposed contract for Request for Qualifications (RFQ) No. 26-015 “Design/Build Services for the Replacement of Existing HVAC System for City of Bryan Fire Station No. 2” with SpawGlass Construction Corp. in an amount not to exceed $1,450,000. 
 Do not approve the proposed contract agreement and provide staff with direction.

 Subject 
 D. Approval of a Contract with May Recreation Equipment & Design, L.P. for the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment for Villa West Park in the amount of $467,855. 
 Type

 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 467,855.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Parkland Dedication Funding (Single Member District 5) 
 Goals 

 Infrastructure
