 Quality of Life 

 Summary: 
 Villa West Park currently features two (2) composite play unit structures. Both play units have been internally inspected by City staff certified in playground safety, and while an immediate hazard to users does not exist, City staff recommends proceeding with replacement of the deteriorating equipment. 

 Installed circa 2000, the playground equipment located within Villa West Park has surpassed its life expectancy and has become the oldest City-owned play equipment in Single Member District 5. This park is heavily used by citizens and visitors throughout the year, resulting in the excessive use of play elements, inevitably promoting deterioration during the last twenty-five-year span. Several replacement parts have become obsolete, thus making any future equipment failures to require specific amenities within the composite structure to be taken out of service. 

 The current fall surfacing for both play units consists of a combination of poured in place (PIP) rubber at the entry points and loose-fill engineered wood fiber (EWF) mulch throughout the remaining square footage. The proposed installation includes a single, unitary material consisting of bonded shredded rubber (BSR) mulch surfacing. This product will improve accessibility to the equipment and maneuverability throughout both play spaces. The proposed installation also features updated shade structures to provide favorable play conditions while increasing the life expectancy of the proposed playground equipment. The two replacement units will serve multiple age groups with one unit designed specifically for users 2-5 years of age and the second designed for users 5-12 years of age. Included in the scope of work is the demolition and removal of the existing play units, shade structures, and surfacing. 

 May Recreation Equipment & Design, L.P. is the selected vendor for the turnkey project, inclusive of removing the existing structures, providing the new units, and complete installation. The selection was based on prior success the City has had with the vendor and the proposal’s effective use of space as well as the high value of the equipment. The proposal’s provision for completely upgrading fall surfaces to meet current industry standards, while also preserving the amount of shade provided over the main equipment structures, significantly improves the overall quality of the play space. Additionally, May Recreation Equipment and Design, L.P. has gone through a competitive bid process for the parks and recreation equipment, products, and installation services as they are a contracted BuyBoard Purchasing Cooperative vendor. The total BuyBoard discount savings for the proposed contract is $52,740. 

 With the replacement of these two play structures, the risk of injury will be significantly reduced and replacement parts will be more readily available to maintain functionality as designed. The new equipment will be more aesthetically pleasing to parkgoers, which in turn, will improve the park system’s infrastructure along with an enhanced quality of life for the community. 

 Currently, this park is included in the City of Bryan and Bryan Independent School District (BISD) Joint Facility Use Agreement as the park is adjacent to Mary Branch Elementary. After communication with BISD staff, City personnel have confirmed that BISD no longer has a vested interest in the playground equipment as both play areas are located outside of the school’s perimeter security fencing installed in 2020. Due to increased security measures, BISD no longer utilizes the playground equipment. Future joint facility use agreements with BISD will not include this property. 

 The cost for equipment and installation will utilize Parkland Dedication funding from Single Member District 5. As of May 7, 2026, the current Parkland Dedication account balance for Single Member District 5 is $697,528.35. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 During the May 19, 2026 Parks and Recreation Advisory Board meeting, a presentation for the equipment replacement, which included renderings for both play areas, was provided. The Board unanimously recommended replacing the playground equipment at Villa West Park with the proposed equipment from May Recreation & Design, L.P. 

 The Parks and Recreation Advisory Board and City staff recommend the City Council approve a contract with May Recreation Equipment & Design, L.P. for the purchase and installation of replacement playground equipment for Villa West Park in the amount of $467,855. 

 Options:

 2) Do not approve the proposed contract and provide staff direction.

Items may be removed from the statutory agenda for separate consideration at the request of two Councilmembers. 
 Subject

 Type

 Dollar Amount 
 1,517,612.31

 Goals 

 Economic Development 

 Infrastructure 

 Service 

 Summary: 
 This project is located at the intersections of Boonville Road (FM158) and Briarcrest Drive (FM1179), Boonville Road (FM158) and Miramont Boulevard, and Green Valley Drive and Briarcrest Drive (FM1179). As part of the Trafalgar Development, the City of Bryan agreed to make improvements to the adjacent intersections. A 380 Agreement exists between the City and the developer for the City to make these improvements. 

 This project is listed in the City of Bryan’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and will install a new traffic signal at the intersection of Boonville Road (FM158) and Miramont Bouldevard, install a new traffic signal at Green Valley Drive and Briarcrest Drive (FM1179), construct a dedicated right-turn lane for northbound traffic on Briarcrest Drive (FM1179) at Green Valley Drive, construct a dedicated right-turn lane for northbound traffic on Briarcrest Drive (FM1179) at Boonville Road (FM158), construct a dedicated right-turn lane for westbound traffic on Boonville Road (FM158) at Briarcrest Drive (FM1179), increase the size of the left-turn bay for westbound traffic on Boonville Road (FM158) at Briarcrest Drive (FM1179), and increase the size of both left-turn bays at the intersection of Miramont Boulevard and Boonville Road. 

 A Request for Proposals (RFP), RFP 26-011, was issued on April 20, 2026, with three (3) bids received by the City on May 12, 2026. Total base bids ranged from $1,517,612.31 to $1,814,049. The bid prices were received as competitive sealed proposals. The proposals were scored by a panel of three City staff and the proposal from Brazos Paving, Inc. scored the highest based on the following criteria: cost proposal, proposed schedule, contractor personnel and personal experience, reputation of contractor/quality assurance, and references. 

 This project is budgeted and is part of a Chapter 380 Agreement between the City of Bryan and the developer. These improvements will help with ingress and egress from the developer's site once improvements are completed. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 
 Staff recommends awarding the traffic signal installation and intersection improvements of the Trafalgar Traffic Signals, City Job Number 750-D7-2412, to Brazos Paving, Inc. in the not to exceed amount of $1,517,612.31. 

 Options: 
 1. Award the proposed contract as recommended 
 2. Award the proposed contract to a different vendor 
 3. Do not award the proposed contract and provide direction to staff

matters.title: D. Consideration, Discussion and Possible Action to Purchase Six (6) Steel Poles for a Transmission Project
matters.body: BTU Board of Directors Regular Meeting
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jun 08, 2026 - BTU Board of Directors Regular Meeting 
 Category 
 7. Regular Session - This agenda consists of items requiring individual consideration by the Board of Directors. 
 Subject 
 D. Consideration, Discussion and Possible Action to Purchase Six (6) Steel Poles for a Transmission Project 
 Type 
 Action, Discussion, Information 
 Preferred Date 
 Jun 08, 2026 
 Absolute Date 
 Jun 08, 2026 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 1,396,452.00 

 Discussion: 

 A new industrial customer is proposing to locate adjacent to the Tabor Substation along Boatcallie Road in Bryan, Texas. The customer has requested electric service at 138kV. 

 To provide 138kV service to the customer, a section of an existing transmission line between Tabor Substation and Rayburn Substation will be converted from 69kV to 138kV and reconfigured to source the customer-owned substation. To maintain the existing Tabor-to-Rayburn transmission connection, BTU will construct a new section of 69kV line on the southwest side of Boatcallie Road. 

 The new section of 69kV line requires six steel transmission poles. Requests for bids were issued on April 17, 2026. Of the five bids received, two were disqualified due to incomplete submittals. The remaining responsive base bids ranged from $1,163,710 to $1,804,629. 

 Techline, Inc. of Austin, Texas (Techline) submitted the lowest responsive bid and took no exceptions or deviations. Techline’s base bid was $1,163,710. Staff is recommending a 20% contingency amount of $232,742, bringing the total not-to-exceed contract amount to $1,396,452. Techline has performed satisfactorily on previous BTU projects, and staff recommends award based on price, responsiveness, and acceptable delivery schedule. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 

 Staff recommends the BTU Board authorize the Board Chair to sign a contract with Techline, Inc. of Austin, Texas in the not-to-exceed amount of $1,396,452 for the purchase of six steel transmission poles needed to support providing 138kV electric service to a new industrial customer near Tabor Substation.

 Type 
 Action (Consent), Discussion, Information 
 Fiscal Impact 
 No 

 Discussion: 

 The BTU Board of Directors approved a contract with Vertexone in January 2026 for a customer portal solution. The project was delayed when BTU experienced a cyber-security incident with its digital bill payment platform provider (also known as, payment processor). While BTU's payment processor was rectifying the cyber-security issue, BTU and Vertexone mutually agreed to delay the portal project kick-off. Vertexone agreed to place a "courtesy hold" on the first milestone payment of implementation fees in the amount of $102,750, with that amount being due upon project kick-off. BTU still had to pay the first installment of subscription fees to Vertexone in the amount of approximately $168,000. This amendment memorializes the verbally agreed upon terms between Vertexone and BTU. 

 Staff Analysis and Recommendation: 

 Staff's recommendation will be contingent upon Legal's discussion in Executive Session.
